# How this file is organised

This file merges what were originally two separate scripts into one. It runs from the raw ESS extract through to every number reported in the project report, so that a reviewer can trace any figure or table in the report back to the code that produced it.

Part 1 is data preparation and the formal analysis. It reads the merged ESS Round 9 and Round 10 extract, builds the analysis sample for the 20 countries that took part in both rounds,
compares item endorsement levels across rounds with survey-weighted regression, estimates the 40 MGM networks, runs the network comparison tests, the exploratory edge-level tests,
the bootstrap accuracy audit and the exploratory community analysis, and writes every result to the caches and CSV files under `multicountry_results/`.

Part 2 is the verification pass. It reads only the CSV files produced by Part 1, together with the raw data, recomputes and prints every number reported in the Results chapter, and draws the figures used in the report.
It re-estimates no network and re-runs no permutation test or bootstrap. The two parts are kept separate on purpose, so that the reported numbers can be checked without repeating any expensive computation.

The expensive steps are controlled by the `RUN_*` switches, all of which are `FALSE` by default. With the caches in place, knitting this file from top to bottom reproduces every reported result in a few minutes.
To recompute from scratch, set the relevant switch to `TRUE`. Be aware that the 40 networks, the 20 network comparison tests, the bootstrap audit and bootEGA each take hours.

## How to run it

Set the working directory to the project root, then knit this file or run it chunk by chunk.
The raw data file `ESS9e03_2-ESS10-subset.csv` must sit in that directory, and the four cached model objects in `multicountry_results/mgm_multicountry_v3/`.

The European Social Survey (ESS) is an academically driven cross-national survey, founded in 2001. It has been administered in 40 countries to date. Its three aims are, firstly – to monitor and interpret changing public attitudes and values within Europe and to investigate how they interact with Europe's changing institutions, secondly – to advance and consolidate improved methods of cross-national survey measurement in Europe and beyond, and thirdly – to develop a series of European social indicators, including attitudinal indicators. The survey involves strict random probability sampling, high response rate and rigorous translation protocols. 

ESS data collection is based on an hour-long face-to-face interview. Due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic at Round 10, a total of 9 countries switched to a self-completion (web and paper) approach, while 22 countries used ESS’s usual face-to-face fieldwork approach. In addition, countries opting for the usual face-to-face approach, could use video interviews as a back-up for the in-person interviews. Caution is advised when making comparisons between countries using face-to-face and self-completion approaches at ESS Round 10, and when making time series comparisons in a country that has used a self-completion approach at Round 10.

Another impact of the pandemic was that Round 10 fieldwork was carried out over a longer period than a usual ESS Round. The first country started fieldwork in September 2020 and the final countries finished fieldwork in August 2022. The pandemic may have resulted in some attitudinal and behavioural changes; therefore, the timing of fieldwork may be particularly important at this round. Users are encouraged to review the fieldwork dates for countries and consider this when carrying out analysis between Round 10 participating countries, or when comparing country level results at Round 10 with previous ESS rounds.

The 21 Basic Human Values items are as follows: 


"Now I will briefly describe some people. Please listen to each description and tell me how much each person is or is not like you. Use this card for your answer."


Thinking up new ideas and being creative is important to him/her. S/he likes to do things in her own original way.

It is important to him/her to be rich. S/he wants to have a lot of money and expensive things.

S/he thinks it is important that every person in the world should be treated equally. S/he believes everyone should have equal opportunities in life.

It's important to him/her to show his/her abilities. S/he wants people to admire what s/he does.

It is important to him/her to live in secure surroundings. S/he avoids anything that might endanger his/her safety.

S/he likes surprises and is always looking for new things to do. S/he thinks it is important to do lots of different things in life.

S/he believes that people should do what they're told. S/he thinks people should follow rules at all times, even when no-one is watching.

It is important to him/her to listen to people who are different from him/her. Even when
s/he disagrees with them, s/he still wants to understand them.

It is important to her to be humble and modest. She tries not to draw attention to herself.

Having a good time is important to her. She likes to “spoil” herself.

It is important to her to make her own decisions about what she does. She likes to be free and not depend on others.

It's very important to her to help the people around her. She wants to care for their well-being.

Being very successful is important to her.She hopes people will recognise her achievements.

It is important to her that the government ensures her safety against all threats. She wants the state to be strong so it can defend its citizens.

She looks for adventures and likes to take risks. She wants to have an exciting life.

It is important to her always to behave properly. She wants to avoid doing anything people would say is wrong.

It is important to her to get respect from others. She wants people to do what she says.

It is important to her to be loyal to her friends. She wants to devote herself to people close to her.

She strongly believes that people should care for nature. Looking after the environment is important to her.

Tradition is important to her. She tries to follow the customs handed down by her religion or her family.

She seeks every chance she can to have fun. It is important to her to do things that give her pleasure.

## Reading and preprocessing the data

```{r data-prep}
pacman::p_load(haven,       # To import different data types
               magrittr,    # For the %<>% operator
               mgm,         # Analyze Mixed Graphical Models
               NetworkComparisonTest,  # Compare networks
               osfr,        # Download OSF data
               qgraph,      # Create stunning network figures
               psych,       # Calculate summary statistics
               sjPlot,      # Many useful data manipulation and data viz functions
               tidyverse,    # Manipulate data the 'tidy' way
               bootnet,      # nonparametric bootstrap
               EGAnet,       # EGA / bootEGA
               survey        # survey-weighted regression and design-based standard errors
               )

## Import the ESS - Round 9 and 10 
## (v3.2 F2F - 22 Countries and v3.1 Self-Completion - 9 Countries)   
df <- read.csv('ESS9e03_2-ESS10-subset.csv')
names(df)

## Subset the data (keeping only variables needed for network analysis)
## Remove missing values (that causes error messages)
df.sub <- df %>%
  select(impdiff:ipudrst,  # BHV items
         essround, # Round (Wave 9 or 10)
         cntry # Country
         ) %>%
  drop_na()  # Remove any NAs

## There are 21 Basic Human Values
names(df.sub)

## Current response options
## 1	Very much like me
## 2	Like me
## 3	Somewhat like me
## 4	A little like me
## 5	Not like me
## 6	Not like me at all

## Reverse code value statements so 6 = 'very much like me'
df.sub %<>%
    mutate(across(impdiff:ipudrst, 
              ~ case_when(. == '1' ~ 6, 
                          . == '2' ~ 5, 
                          . == '3' ~ 4, 
                          . == '4' ~ 3, 
                          . == '5' ~ 2, 
                          . == '6' ~ 1)
      )
    )

sumstats <- df.sub %>% 
  describeBy(group = c('essround','cntry'),
              mat = TRUE) 

## Function to subset by country
table(df.sub$cntry)
countries <- df.sub %>% 
  distinct(cntry) %>%
  unlist()

## Prepare Data for Network Analysis -- Wave 9 
df.store.w9 <- list()
for (i in 1:length(countries)) {
  df.store.w9[[i]] <- df.sub %>%  # Store results of loop in item
    filter(essround == 9 & cntry == countries[[i]]) %>%  # Subset data by country
    select(!c(essround, cntry)) %>% # Remove country name for mgm()
    drop_na() %>%  # Remove any lingering NAs
    data.matrix()  # Convert to numeric matrix
}

## Prepare Data for Network Analysis -- Wave 10
df.store.w10 <- list()
for (i in 1:length(countries)) {
  df.store.w10[[i]] <- df.sub %>%  # Store results of loop in item
    filter(essround == 10 & cntry == countries[[i]]) %>%  # Subset data by country
    select(!c(essround, cntry)) %>% # Remove country name for mgm()
    drop_na() %>%  # Remove any lingering NAs
    data.matrix()  # Convert to numeric matrix
}

```

Testing whether value endorsement differs between the pre-pandemic and pandemic rounds.
Before conducting the network analysis, let's check whether there are statistically significant differences in values pre- and post-pandemic. We could also do this across countries if we were so inclined.


## Comparing item endorsement levels across rounds (survey-weighted regression)

Before any network is estimated, item scores in ESS Round 9 and Round 10 are compared with survey-weighted regression, holding country constant through fixed effects,
with standard errors computed from the ESS analysis weights and the stratified multistage design. This is a free-standing complement to the network analysis. It is **not** a precondition or a screening test for estimating the networks.

```{r level-test}
## ---- 1.1 Fix the item set and the country set -----------------------------

# Pull the names of the 21 value items once and reuse them in every later across()/all_of() call.
# Hard-coding impdiff:ipudrst in several places would mean several places to update if the item set ever changed.
bhv <- df.sub %>%              # df.sub is used only to read column names, not its data
  select(impdiff:ipudrst) %>%  # the 21 items sit in one contiguous block in the data frame
  names()                      # keep the names and discard the data

# The extract holds 31 countries, but only 20 took part in both Round 9 and Round 10.
# The other 11 (AT/CY/DE/DK/ES/LV/PL/RS/SE in R9 only; GR/MK in R10 only) cannot be compared across rounds,
# and if they were left in, the NCT loop below would be handed a zero-row matrix and fail.
countries.both <- df.sub %>%
  distinct(cntry, essround) %>%  # one row per country-by-round combination
  count(cntry) %>%               # how many rounds each country appears in, 1 or 2
  filter(n == 2) %>%             # keep only the countries present in both rounds
  pull(cntry) %>%                # extract as a character vector
  sort()                         # sorting fixes the loop order, so output tables are reproducible row for row

length(countries.both)           # expected: 20
countries.both                   # printed so the country list can be checked by eye

## ---- 1.2 Rebuild the analysis data with the design variables ---------------

# Why df.sub cannot be reused here:
#  (1) its select() kept only the 21 items plus essround and cntry, so anweight, stratum and psu
#      were dropped;
#  (2) its drop_na() ran BEFORE reverse coding, and codes 7/8/9 only become NA during reverse
#      coding, so df.sub still carries those missing values
#      (only df.store.w9/w10 drop them a second time inside their loops, so only those lists are clean).
# The data are therefore rebuilt from the raw df, with the order corrected: reverse code first, then drop missing.
df.svy <- df %>%
  select(all_of(bhv), essround, cntry, anweight, stratum, psu) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(bhv),
                ~ case_when(. == 1 ~ 6,
                            . == 2 ~ 5,
                            . == 3 ~ 4,
                            . == 4 ~ 3,
                            . == 5 ~ 2,
                            . == 6 ~ 1))) %>%
  drop_na(all_of(bhv)) %>%
  filter(cntry %in% countries.both) %>%
  mutate(
    r10   = as.numeric(essround == 10),   # round dummy: R9 = 0 (reference), R10 = 1
    cntry = factor(cntry),                # as a factor, svyglm expands this into 19 country dummies

    # Stratum ID: built with paste rather than interaction().
    # interaction() builds the full cartesian product of levels before discarding the empty ones, even with drop = TRUE;
    # paste is O(n) and touches only the 62755 rows, so its cost is negligible.
    strat_id = factor(paste(cntry, essround, stratum, sep = "_")),

    # PSU ID: stratum is pasted in as well, so each PSU is explicitly nested within its stratum.
    # That is exactly what nest = TRUE would do, which is why nest must be set to FALSE below.
    # Left at TRUE, survey calls interaction() again on about 4600 by about 31800 levels,
    # attempting to build 146 million label strings (roughly 8 GB), which is what made an earlier run hang.
    psu_id   = factor(paste(cntry, essround, stratum, psu, sep = "_"))
  )

nrow(df.svy)            # expected: 62755
table(df.svy$essround)  # expected: 31687 in R9 and 31068 in R10

## ---- Build the survey design object ---------------------------------------

# Finland (about 877/788 strata) and Iceland (347/372) necessarily contain strata holding a single PSU.
# survey cannot compute a within-stratum variance for those and stops with an error by default. "adjust" substitutes
# the population mean for the stratum mean, which is the conservative choice (it inflates the variance). It affects every standard error reported here and is stated in the Methods chapter and in Appendix C2.
options(survey.lonely.psu = "adjust")

des <- svydesign(ids     = ~psu_id,    # PSU already includes stratum, so IDs are globally unique and explicitly nested
                 strata  = ~strat_id,  # stratification variable
                 weights = ~anweight,  # ESS analysis weight = pspwght x pweight
                 data    = df.svy,
                 nest    = FALSE)      # critical: IDs are already unique, and TRUE triggers the cartesian blow-up described above

degf(des)   # design degrees of freedom = number of PSUs minus number of strata; printing a number here confirms the design is usable

## ---- 1.4 One weighted regression per item ---------------------------------

# Model: item ~ r10 + cntry
#   The r10 coefficient compares the two rounds WITHIN country, then averages across countries by weight.
#   Country fixed effects are included to condition out the change in country composition between rounds:
#   the UK sample falls from 2122 to 1102 and the Bulgarian sample rises from 1503 to 2545, and without
#   country controls those compositional shifts would be read as changes in values.

lvl.res <- bind_rows(lapply(bhv, function(v) {  # one regression per item, results stacked into a single table

  # paste0 builds a string such as "impdiff ~ r10 + cntry", which as.formula turns into a formula object
  fit <- svyglm(as.formula(paste0(v, " ~ r10 + cntry")), design = des)

  # The r10 row of the coefficient table: a named vector of Estimate / Std. Error / t value / Pr(>|t|)
  s  <- summary(fit)$coefficients["r10", ]

  # Design-based 95% confidence interval; confint.svyglm uses degf(des) for the degrees of freedom
  ci <- confint(fit)["r10", ]

  # Weighted population variance pooled over both rounds. Its square root is the standard deviation used to
  # convert the raw score difference into a standardised effect size. svyvar returns a 1x1 matrix here.
  sdp <- sqrt(as.numeric(svyvar(as.formula(paste0("~", v)), des)))

  tibble(item    = v,                 # item variable name
         b       = s[["Estimate"]],   # raw score difference R10 minus R9, in scale points (1-6), directly interpretable
         se      = s[["Std. Error"]], # design-based standard error (stratification, clustering and weights all accounted for)
         ci_lo   = ci[[1]],           # lower 95% CI bound, raw score scale
         ci_hi   = ci[[2]],           # upper 95% CI bound, raw score scale
         sd_pool = sdp,               # pooled weighted standard deviation, the denominator of the standardisation
         d       = b     / sdp,       # standardised effect size, comparable across items and to the literature
         d_lo    = ci_lo / sdp,       # lower CI bound on the effect size (a linear rescaling, so simple division is exact)
         d_hi    = ci_hi / sdp,       # upper CI bound on the effect size
         p_raw   = s[["Pr(>|t|)"]])   # unadjusted p value
}))

# The 21 items form one family of tests, so the family-wise error rate has to be controlled.
# Holm and Bonferroni control the same quantity (FWER), but Holm is uniformly more powerful, so Holm is what the report uses.
lvl.res <- lvl.res %>%
  mutate(p_holm = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "holm"),
         p_bonf = p.adjust(p_raw, method = "bonferroni")) %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(d)))   # largest absolute effect sizes first, so the items worth attention head the table

print(lvl.res, n = 21)                                            # all 21 rows
write.csv(lvl.res, "level_test_weighted.csv", row.names = FALSE)  # written out for the report tables and for Part 2

## ---- 1.5 Note on the figure ------------------------------------------------

# Figure 4 of the report (standardised round differences for the 21 items) is drawn in the plotting section of Part 2,
# where the shared theme, palette and item labels live, so that one figure never appears in two different styles.
# This chunk is responsible only for writing level_test_weighted.csv, which that section reads back.




```

## Restoring the signs of the edge weights

`mgm()` stores edge magnitude and edge sign separately, in `pairwise$wadj` and `pairwise$signs`.
Every network in the formal pipeline uses the sign-restored adjacency matrix, so the step is written once as a function and reused throughout. Anyone checking a reported edge weight should apply this same function.

```{r signed-wadj}
get_signed_wadj <- function(model) {
  W <- model$pairwise$wadj * model$pairwise$signs
  diag(W) <- 0
  W[is.na(W)] <- 0
  W
}
```

## Formal analysis of the 20 countries

What follows is the formal pipeline for the study as planned. The target of inference is always the full set of 20 countries with PVQ-21 data in both rounds.
The countries shown as examples in the report are chosen only after all formal results are complete, and are used for illustrative plotting alone. They play no part in sample selection, model estimation, the NCT or the multiple-comparison correction.

### 1. Estimate and cache the 40 formal MGM networks

```{r multicountry-main-networks}
## ---- 1.0 All formal parameters defined in one place -----------------------

ANALYSIS_VERSION <- "mgm_multicountry_v3"
MGM_K             <- 2L
MGM_LAMBDA_GAM    <- 0.50
MGM_LAMBDA_SEL    <- "EBIC"
MGM_RULE           <- "AND"
MGM_THRESHOLD      <- "LW"
MGM_SCALE          <- TRUE
MGM_BINARY_SIGN    <- FALSE  # all 21 nodes are treated as Gaussian, so binarySign does not apply here
NETWORK_SEED_BASE <- 20260825L
CHANGE_TOL        <- 1e-12

RESULT_DIR <- file.path("multicountry_results", ANALYSIS_VERSION)
dir.create(RESULT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

stopifnot(length(countries.both) == 20L)
stopifnot(length(bhv) == 21L)

## Every country uses the same node order and the same complete-case rule
make_network_data <- function(round_no) {
  out <- lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
    df.sub %>%
      filter(essround == round_no, cntry == cc) %>%
      select(all_of(bhv)) %>%
      drop_na() %>%
      data.matrix()
  })
  names(out) <- countries.both
  out
}

d9  <- make_network_data(9)
d10 <- make_network_data(10)

sample_sizes <- tibble(
  cntry = countries.both,
  n9    = vapply(d9, nrow, integer(1)),
  n10   = vapply(d10, nrow, integer(1))
)

if (any(sample_sizes$n9 == 0L | sample_sizes$n10 == 0L)) {
  stop("At least one included country has no complete cases in one wave; formal analysis cannot continue.", call. = FALSE)
}
if (any(vapply(c(d9, d10), ncol, integer(1)) != length(bhv))) {
  stop("At least one country-wave dataset does not contain 21 nodes; formal analysis cannot continue.", call. = FALSE)
}

## The data signature exists to stop the script silently reading a stale cache after the data or the parameters change
data_signature <- list(
  n9    = vapply(d9, nrow, integer(1)),
  n10   = vapply(d10, nrow, integer(1)),
  sum9  = vapply(d9,  function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1)),
  sum10 = vapply(d10, function(x) sum(x, na.rm = TRUE), numeric(1))
)

network_metadata <- list(
  analysis_version = ANALYSIS_VERSION,
  countries        = countries.both,
  nodes            = bhv,
  k                = MGM_K,
  lambda_sel       = MGM_LAMBDA_SEL,
  lambda_gam       = MGM_LAMBDA_GAM,
  rule             = MGM_RULE,
  threshold        = MGM_THRESHOLD,
  scale            = MGM_SCALE,
  binary_sign      = MGM_BINARY_SIGN,
  data_signature   = data_signature,
  r_version        = R.version.string,
  mgm_version      = as.character(packageVersion("mgm"))
)

fit_mgm_network <- function(data) {
  fit <- mgm(
    data      = data,
    type      = rep("g", ncol(data)),
    level     = rep(1, ncol(data)),
    k         = MGM_K,
    lambdaSel = MGM_LAMBDA_SEL,
    lambdaGam = MGM_LAMBDA_GAM,
    ruleReg   = MGM_RULE,
    threshold = MGM_THRESHOLD,
    scale     = MGM_SCALE,
    binarySign = MGM_BINARY_SIGN
  )

  W <- get_signed_wadj(fit)
  rownames(W) <- colnames(W) <- bhv

  if (!all(dim(W) == c(length(bhv), length(bhv)))) {
    stop("The adjacency matrix has incorrect dimensions.")
  }
  if (max(abs(W - t(W))) > 1e-10) {
    stop("The adjacency matrix is not symmetric.")
  }
  if (any(!is.finite(W)) || any(diag(W) != 0)) {
    stop("The adjacency matrix contains non-finite values or a non-zero diagonal.")
  }

  list(model = fit, W = W)
}

NETWORK_CACHE_FILE <- file.path(RESULT_DIR, "mgm_network_cache.rds")

if (file.exists(NETWORK_CACHE_FILE)) {
  network_cache <- readRDS(NETWORK_CACHE_FILE)
  if (!identical(network_cache$metadata, network_metadata)) {
    warning("The formal-network cache does not match the current data or parameters and has been reset.")
    network_cache <- list(metadata = network_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
  }
} else {
  network_cache <- list(metadata = network_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
}

## Save after every country, so an interrupted run only has to re-fit the countries that have not yet succeeded
for (cc in countries.both) {
  if (!is.null(network_cache$results[[cc]])) next

  message("Formal MGM networks: ", cc,
          " (n9 = ", nrow(d9[[cc]]), ", n10 = ", nrow(d10[[cc]]), ")")
  set.seed(NETWORK_SEED_BASE + match(cc, countries.both))

  one_country <- tryCatch(
    list(
      R9  = fit_mgm_network(d9[[cc]]),
      R10 = fit_mgm_network(d10[[cc]])
    ),
    error = function(e) structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)), class = "network_fit_error")
  )

  if (inherits(one_country, "network_fit_error")) {
    network_cache$errors[[cc]] <- one_country$message
  } else {
    network_cache$results[[cc]] <- one_country
    network_cache$errors[[cc]] <- NULL
  }
  saveRDS(network_cache, NETWORK_CACHE_FILE)
}

missing_networks <- setdiff(countries.both, names(network_cache$results))
if (length(missing_networks) > 0L) {
  error_text <- vapply(missing_networks, function(cc) {
    error_message <- network_cache$errors[[cc]]
    if (is.null(error_message)) error_message <- "Unknown error"
    paste0(cc, ": ", error_message)
  }, character(1))
  stop(paste("Formal network estimation has not succeeded for the following countries:", paste(error_text, collapse = "; ")),
       call. = FALSE)
}

## Models and sign-restored matrices are cached separately, because the NCT, the plotting, the difference networks and the audit each reuse them
network_models_all <- setNames(lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
  list(R9  = network_cache$results[[cc]]$R9$model,
       R10 = network_cache$results[[cc]]$R10$model)
}), countries.both)

signed_networks_all <- setNames(lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
  list(R9  = network_cache$results[[cc]]$R9$W,
       R10 = network_cache$results[[cc]]$R10$W)
}), countries.both)

saveRDS(network_models_all, file.path(RESULT_DIR, "mgm_models_40.rds"))
saveRDS(signed_networks_all, file.path(RESULT_DIR, "signed_networks_40.rds"))

## Per-network diagnostics. All 40 rows must pass before any of these results are written up
network_diagnostics <- bind_rows(lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
  bind_rows(lapply(c("R9", "R10"), function(wave) {
    W <- signed_networks_all[[cc]][[wave]]
    edge_values <- W[upper.tri(W)]
    tibble(
      cntry              = cc,
      wave               = wave,
      n                  = if (wave == "R9") nrow(d9[[cc]]) else nrow(d10[[cc]]),
      n_nodes            = nrow(W),
      symmetric          = max(abs(W - t(W))) <= 1e-10,
      zero_diagonal      = all(diag(W) == 0),
      all_finite         = all(is.finite(W)),
      n_edges            = sum(abs(edge_values) > CHANGE_TOL),
      n_positive_edges   = sum(edge_values > CHANGE_TOL),
      n_negative_edges   = sum(edge_values < -CHANGE_TOL),
      global_strength    = sum(abs(edge_values)),
      mean_present_edge  = ifelse(sum(abs(edge_values) > CHANGE_TOL) == 0L,
                                  NA_real_,
                                  mean(abs(edge_values[abs(edge_values) > CHANGE_TOL])))
    )
  }))
}))

if (!all(network_diagnostics$symmetric &
         network_diagnostics$zero_diagonal &
         network_diagnostics$all_finite &
         network_diagnostics$n_nodes == length(bhv))) {
  stop("At least one of the 40 networks failed the matrix diagnostics.", call. = FALSE)
}

write.csv(network_diagnostics,
          file.path(RESULT_DIR, "network_diagnostics_40.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

## Descriptive global properties for all 20 countries
global_props_all <- network_diagnostics %>%
  select(cntry, wave, n, n_edges, global_strength, mean_present_edge) %>%
  mutate(density = n_edges / choose(length(bhv), 2)) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = wave,
              values_from = c(n, n_edges, density, global_strength, mean_present_edge)) %>%
  mutate(global_strength_diff = global_strength_R10 - global_strength_R9)

write.csv(global_props_all,
          file.path(RESULT_DIR, "global_properties_20countries.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
print(global_props_all, n = 20)
```

### 2. Build the 20 signed difference networks and describe them across countries

```{r multicountry-signed-differences}
## The difference is always defined as R10 minus R9. A positive value means the conditional association moved in the positive direction, a negative value the reverse
difference_networks_all <- setNames(lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
  signed_networks_all[[cc]]$R10 - signed_networks_all[[cc]]$R9
}), countries.both)

saveRDS(difference_networks_all,
        file.path(RESULT_DIR, "signed_difference_networks_20.rds"))

edge_index <- which(upper.tri(matrix(0, length(bhv), length(bhv))), arr.ind = TRUE)

difference_vectors <- do.call(rbind, lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
  difference_networks_all[[cc]][upper.tri(difference_networks_all[[cc]])]
}))
rownames(difference_vectors) <- countries.both
colnames(difference_vectors) <- paste0(
  bhv[edge_index[, 1]], "__", bhv[edge_index[, 2]]
)

## Edge-level summary across countries. Direction and magnitude are reported; p values are never averaged across countries
edge_delta_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(seq_len(nrow(edge_index)), function(i) {
  delta <- difference_vectors[, i]
  tibble(
    node1              = paste0("V", edge_index[i, 1]),
    node2              = paste0("V", edge_index[i, 2]),
    item1              = bhv[edge_index[i, 1]],
    item2              = bhv[edge_index[i, 2]],
    median_delta       = median(delta),
    mean_delta         = mean(delta),
    mean_abs_delta     = mean(abs(delta)),
    min_delta          = min(delta),
    max_delta          = max(delta),
    n_positive_change  = sum(delta > CHANGE_TOL),
    n_negative_change  = sum(delta < -CHANGE_TOL),
    n_no_change        = sum(abs(delta) <= CHANGE_TOL)
  )
}))

write.csv(edge_delta_summary,
          file.path(RESULT_DIR, "cross_country_signed_edge_changes.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)

## Country-level change magnitudes are descriptive only. They order countries by how much moved, not by significance, and are used to pick the illustrative case
median_change_pattern <- apply(difference_vectors, 2, median)

country_change_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
  delta <- difference_vectors[cc, ]
  tibble(
    cntry                    = cc,
    n9                       = nrow(d9[[cc]]),
    n10                      = nrow(d10[[cc]]),
    mean_signed_edge_change  = mean(delta),
    median_signed_edge_change = median(delta),
    mean_abs_edge_change     = mean(abs(delta)),
    max_abs_edge_change      = max(abs(delta)),
    l2_change                = sqrt(sum(delta^2)),
    distance_to_median_pattern = sqrt(sum((delta - median_change_pattern)^2)),
    n_positive_change        = sum(delta > CHANGE_TOL),
    n_negative_change        = sum(delta < -CHANGE_TOL),
    n_no_change              = sum(abs(delta) <= CHANGE_TOL)
  )
}))

write.csv(country_change_summary,
          file.path(RESULT_DIR, "country_change_patterns_20.csv"),
          row.names = FALSE)
print(country_change_summary, n = 20)
```

### 3. Formal NCT for all 20 countries

The low-iteration test run exists only to confirm that the function and the cache work. It produces no country ranking and takes no part in choosing the illustrative case.
For a real run, set `RUN_NCT_FORMAL` to `TRUE`. If the run is interrupted it resumes from the countries already completed.

```{r multicountry-formal-nct}
NCT_IT_TEST       <- 20L
NCT_IT_FORMAL     <- 1000L
NCT_SEED_BASE     <- 20261825L
RUN_NCT_TEST      <- FALSE
RUN_NCT_FORMAL    <- FALSE

## The main NCT tests overall structure and global strength only.
## The exploratory test of all 210 edges is run separately; dropping countries is not an acceptable way to save computation.
nct_estimator_mgm <- function(data, ...) {
  fit_mgm_network(data)$W
}

run_nct_one <- function(cc, iterations) {
  NCT(
    d9[[cc]],
    d10[[cc]],
    it              = iterations,
    binary.data     = FALSE,
    paired          = FALSE,
    abs             = TRUE,
    test.edges      = FALSE,
    test.centrality = FALSE,
    estimator       = nct_estimator_mgm,
    progressbar     = FALSE,
    verbose         = FALSE
  )
}

## Pipeline test: always the first country in the list, and never saved as a formal result
if (RUN_NCT_TEST) {
  NCT_TEST_COUNTRY <- countries.both[1]
  set.seed(NCT_SEED_BASE + match(NCT_TEST_COUNTRY, countries.both))
  nct_pipeline_test <- run_nct_one(NCT_TEST_COUNTRY, NCT_IT_TEST)
  message("The NCT pipeline test is complete; this result must not be reported or used to select countries.")
}

nct_metadata <- list(
  analysis_version = ANALYSIS_VERSION,
  countries        = countries.both,
  nodes            = bhv,
  mgm_k            = MGM_K,
  lambda_sel       = MGM_LAMBDA_SEL,
  lambda_gam       = MGM_LAMBDA_GAM,
  mgm_rule         = MGM_RULE,
  mgm_threshold    = MGM_THRESHOLD,
  mgm_scale        = MGM_SCALE,
  mgm_binary_sign  = MGM_BINARY_SIGN,
  iterations       = NCT_IT_FORMAL,
  paired           = FALSE,
  abs              = TRUE,
  test_edges       = FALSE,
  data_signature   = data_signature,
  nct_version      = as.character(packageVersion("NetworkComparisonTest"))
)

NCT_FORMAL_FILE <- file.path(
  RESULT_DIR,
  paste0("nct_formal_all20_it", NCT_IT_FORMAL, "_no_edge_tests.rds")
)

if (file.exists(NCT_FORMAL_FILE)) {
  nct_cache <- readRDS(NCT_FORMAL_FILE)
  if (!identical(nct_cache$metadata, nct_metadata)) {
    warning("The NCT cache does not match the current data or parameters and has been reset.")
    nct_cache <- list(metadata = nct_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
  }
} else {
  nct_cache <- list(metadata = nct_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
}

if (RUN_NCT_FORMAL) {
  for (cc in countries.both) {
    if (!is.null(nct_cache$results[[cc]])) next

    message("Formal NCT: ", cc,
            " (n9 = ", nrow(d9[[cc]]), ", n10 = ", nrow(d10[[cc]]), ")")
    set.seed(NCT_SEED_BASE + match(cc, countries.both))

    one_nct <- tryCatch(
      run_nct_one(cc, NCT_IT_FORMAL),
      error = function(e) structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)), class = "nct_fit_error")
    )

    if (inherits(one_nct, "nct_fit_error")) {
      nct_cache$errors[[cc]] <- one_nct$message
    } else {
      nct_cache$results[[cc]] <- one_nct
      nct_cache$errors[[cc]] <- NULL
    }
    saveRDS(nct_cache, NCT_FORMAL_FILE)
  }
}

nct_completed_countries <- intersect(countries.both, names(nct_cache$results))
NCT_FORMAL_COMPLETE <- setequal(nct_completed_countries, countries.both)

nct_result_row <- function(cc) {
  x <- nct_cache$results[[cc]]
  tibble(
    cntry        = cc,
    n9           = nrow(d9[[cc]]),
    n10          = nrow(d10[[cc]]),
    M            = as.numeric(x$nwinv.real),
    p_struct_raw = as.numeric(x$nwinv.pval),
    S_R9         = as.numeric(x$glstrinv.sep[1]),
    S_R10        = as.numeric(x$glstrinv.sep[2]),
    S_diff       = as.numeric(x$glstrinv.sep[2] - x$glstrinv.sep[1]),
    p_global_raw = as.numeric(x$glstrinv.pval)
  )
}

if (length(nct_completed_countries) > 0L) {
  nct.res <- bind_rows(lapply(nct_completed_countries, nct_result_row))
} else {
  nct.res <- tibble()
}

if (NCT_FORMAL_COMPLETE) {
  nct.res <- nct.res %>%
    arrange(match(cntry, countries.both)) %>%
    mutate(
      p_struct_holm = p.adjust(p_struct_raw, method = "holm"),
      p_global_holm = p.adjust(p_global_raw, method = "holm")
    )

  write.csv(nct.res,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "nct_formal_summary_all20_mgm.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
  print(nct.res, n = 20)
} else {
  message("Formal NCT has not yet covered all 20 countries: completed ",
          length(nct_completed_countries), "/20. No formal summary CSV or cross-country adjusted p-values were generated.")
}
```

### 4. Exploratory NCT for all 210 edges in all 20 countries

The edge-level tests take no part in choosing countries and never use `DISPLAY_COUNTRIES`. They are run separately, after the overall NCT has finished for all 20 countries,
and Holm correction is reported at two levels: within each country across its 210 edges, and across all 4200 tests. With 1000 permutations the smallest
resolvable p value is about `1/1001`, so Holm correction over 4200 tests can almost never reject at this number of permutations.
These results are therefore treated as exploratory. Signed differences and unbinarised p values are reported side by side, and countries are never ranked by a count of significant edges.

```{r multicountry-exploratory-edge-nct}
RUN_EDGE_NCT_EXPLORATORY <- FALSE
NCT_IT_EDGES              <- 1000L
NCT_EDGE_SEED_BASE        <- 20262825L

edge_nct_metadata <- list(
  analysis_version = ANALYSIS_VERSION,
  countries        = countries.both,
  nodes            = bhv,
  mgm_k            = MGM_K,
  lambda_sel       = MGM_LAMBDA_SEL,
  lambda_gam       = MGM_LAMBDA_GAM,
  mgm_rule         = MGM_RULE,
  mgm_threshold    = MGM_THRESHOLD,
  mgm_scale        = MGM_SCALE,
  mgm_binary_sign  = MGM_BINARY_SIGN,
  iterations       = NCT_IT_EDGES,
  paired           = FALSE,
  abs              = TRUE,
  test_edges       = TRUE,
  edges            = "all",
  p_adjust_inside_nct = "none",
  data_signature   = data_signature,
  nct_version      = as.character(packageVersion("NetworkComparisonTest"))
)

NCT_EDGE_FILE <- file.path(
  RESULT_DIR,
  paste0("nct_edges_all20_it", NCT_IT_EDGES, "_raw_p.rds")
)

if (file.exists(NCT_EDGE_FILE)) {
  edge_nct_cache <- readRDS(NCT_EDGE_FILE)
  if (!identical(edge_nct_cache$metadata, edge_nct_metadata)) {
    warning("The edge-level NCT cache does not match the current data or parameters and has been reset.")
    edge_nct_cache <- list(metadata = edge_nct_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
  }
} else {
  edge_nct_cache <- list(metadata = edge_nct_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
}

run_edge_nct_one <- function(cc) {
  NCT(
    d9[[cc]],
    d10[[cc]],
    it               = NCT_IT_EDGES,
    binary.data      = FALSE,
    paired           = FALSE,
    abs              = TRUE,
    test.edges       = TRUE,
    edges            = "all",
    p.adjust.methods = "none",  # keep the raw p values here; both levels of Holm correction are applied once, in the results table below
    test.centrality  = FALSE,
    estimator        = nct_estimator_mgm,
    progressbar      = FALSE,
    verbose          = FALSE
  )
}

if (RUN_EDGE_NCT_EXPLORATORY && !NCT_FORMAL_COMPLETE) {
  stop("The formal overall NCT must be completed for all 20 countries before running edge-level exploration.", call. = FALSE)
}

if (RUN_EDGE_NCT_EXPLORATORY) {
  for (cc in countries.both) {
    if (!is.null(edge_nct_cache$results[[cc]])) next

    message("Exploratory all-edge NCT: ", cc, " (210 edges)")
    set.seed(NCT_EDGE_SEED_BASE + match(cc, countries.both))

    one_edge_nct <- tryCatch(
      run_edge_nct_one(cc),
      error = function(e) structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)), class = "edge_nct_error")
    )

    if (inherits(one_edge_nct, "edge_nct_error")) {
      edge_nct_cache$errors[[cc]] <- one_edge_nct$message
    } else {
      edge_nct_cache$results[[cc]] <- one_edge_nct
      edge_nct_cache$errors[[cc]] <- NULL
    }
    saveRDS(edge_nct_cache, NCT_EDGE_FILE)
  }
}

edge_nct_completed <- intersect(countries.both, names(edge_nct_cache$results))
EDGE_NCT_COMPLETE <- setequal(edge_nct_completed, countries.both)

extract_edge_nct_table <- function(cc) {
  edge_table <- as.data.frame(edge_nct_cache$results[[cc]]$einv.pvals)
  if (ncol(edge_table) < 3L) {
    stop(paste0("The einv.pvals output for ", cc, " has an unexpected format: fewer than three columns."))
  }

  names_lower <- tolower(names(edge_table))
  p_col <- grep("p.?value|^p$", names_lower)[1]
  if (is.na(p_col)) p_col <- 3L

  raw_node1 <- as.character(edge_table[[1]])
  raw_node2 <- as.character(edge_table[[2]])
  i <- match(raw_node1, bhv)
  j <- match(raw_node2, bhv)

  if (anyNA(i) || anyNA(j)) {
    stop(paste0("The edge-level NCT node names for ", cc, " cannot be matched to the bhv node order."))
  }

  # Careful: the new columns below must not also be called node1/node2 and then referenced as item1 = node1.
  # Inside tibble(), a later argument can see columns created by an earlier one, exactly as in a mutate() chain.
  # If the new columns were named node1/node2, item1 = node1 would read the "V10"-style column just created
  # rather than the original item name, which is why an earlier run produced item1/item2 columns that merely duplicated node1/node2.
  # Using raw_node1/raw_node2, names that cannot collide with the tibble's own columns, preserves the real item names.
  tibble(
    cntry = cc,
    node1 = paste0("V", i),
    node2 = paste0("V", j),
    item1 = raw_node1,
    item2 = raw_node2,
    delta_R10_minus_R9 = difference_networks_all[[cc]][cbind(i, j)],
    abs_delta = abs(delta_R10_minus_R9),
    p_edge_raw = as.numeric(edge_table[[p_col]])
  )
}

if (EDGE_NCT_COMPLETE) {
  edge_nct_results <- bind_rows(lapply(countries.both, extract_edge_nct_table)) %>%
    group_by(cntry) %>%
    mutate(p_edge_holm_within_country = p.adjust(p_edge_raw, method = "holm")) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(p_edge_holm_all_4200 = p.adjust(p_edge_raw, method = "holm")) %>%
    arrange(cntry, p_edge_raw)

  if (nrow(edge_nct_results) != length(countries.both) * choose(length(bhv), 2)) {
    stop("The all-edge NCT output is not 20 countries x 210 edges; incomplete results will not be exported.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  write.csv(edge_nct_results,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "nct_edges_exploratory_all20.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  edge_nct_country_summary <- edge_nct_results %>%
    group_by(cntry) %>%
    summarise(
      min_p_raw = min(p_edge_raw),
      n_within_country_holm_below_05 = sum(p_edge_holm_within_country < .05),
      median_abs_delta = median(abs_delta),
      max_abs_delta = max(abs_delta),
      .groups = "drop"
    )

  write.csv(edge_nct_country_summary,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "nct_edges_exploratory_country_summary.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  message("Exploratory edge NCT has not yet covered all 20 countries: completed ", length(edge_nct_completed),
          "/20. No complete all-edge summary CSV was generated.")
}
```

### 5. The illustrative case is chosen only after all formal results exist

```{r display-countries-after-formal-analysis}
## DISPLAY_COUNTRIES may be used for plotting only. It must never enter estimation, the NCT or any multiple-comparison correction
if (NCT_FORMAL_COMPLETE) {
  ## All 20 countries are ranked on the same Euclidean distance measure. No country holds a reserved display slot
  display_pool <- country_change_summary

  if (nrow(display_pool) != length(countries.both) ||
      !setequal(display_pool$cntry, countries.both)) {
    stop("The display-country candidate pool does not contain exactly the complete 20-country analysis set.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  display_selection <- display_pool %>%
    arrange(distance_to_median_pattern, cntry) %>%
    mutate(
      distance_rank = row_number(),
      case_group = case_when(
        distance_rank <= 3L ~ "Closest 3",
        distance_rank > n() - 3L ~ "Farthest 3",
        TRUE ~ "Middle"
      ),
      selection_rule = paste0(
        "Ascending Euclidean distance from the all-20-country median edge-change pattern; ",
        "ties resolved by country code"
      )
    ) %>%
    select(cntry, distance_to_median_pattern, distance_rank,
           case_group, selection_rule)

  if (nrow(display_selection) != 20L ||
      n_distinct(display_selection$cntry) != 20L ||
      !identical(display_selection$distance_rank, seq_len(20L))) {
    stop("The display-country ranking did not produce 20 unique countries with ranks 1 through 20.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (sum(display_selection$case_group == "Closest 3") != 3L ||
      sum(display_selection$case_group == "Middle") != 14L ||
      sum(display_selection$case_group == "Farthest 3") != 3L) {
    stop("The display-country grouping is not 3 closest, 14 middle, and 3 farthest countries.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  DISPLAY_COUNTRIES <- display_selection$cntry

  write.csv(display_selection,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "display_country_selection.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
} else {
  ## Until the formal NCT is complete, no display country is chosen and no fallback case is substituted
  DISPLAY_COUNTRIES <- character(0)
  display_selection <- tibble(
    cntry = character(),
    distance_to_median_pattern = numeric(),
    distance_rank = integer(),
    case_group = character(),
    selection_rule = character()
  )
  message("Formal NCT for all 20 countries is incomplete; no display country was selected.")
}

print(display_selection)

RUN_DISPLAY_FIGURES <- FALSE

if (RUN_DISPLAY_FIGURES) {
  FIGURE_DIR <- file.path(RESULT_DIR, "display_figures_all20_common_scale")
  dir.create(FIGURE_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  ## Node positions are fixed by all 40 R9/R10 formal networks together. The difference networks take no part in the layout
  formal_networks_for_layout <- unname(unlist(
    lapply(countries.both, function(cc) signed_networks_all[[cc]][c("R9", "R10")]),
    recursive = FALSE
  ))
  set.seed(NETWORK_SEED_BASE + 3000L)
  common_layout_all <- do.call(averageLayout, formal_networks_for_layout)

  ## The 40 formal networks and the 20 difference networks share one edge-width scale, so the plots are comparable across countries
  all_plot_networks <- c(
    formal_networks_for_layout,
    unname(difference_networks_all[countries.both])
  )
  global_maximum_all <- max(
    vapply(all_plot_networks, function(W) max(abs(W)), numeric(1)),
    .Machine$double.eps
  )

  if (!all(dim(common_layout_all) == c(length(bhv), 2L)) ||
      any(!is.finite(common_layout_all))) {
    stop("The common 20-country node layout is invalid.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (!is.finite(global_maximum_all) || global_maximum_all <= 0) {
    stop("The common 20-country edge-weight maximum is invalid.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  for (cc in DISPLAY_COUNTRIES) {
    W9    <- signed_networks_all[[cc]]$R9
    W10   <- signed_networks_all[[cc]]$R10
    Wdiff <- difference_networks_all[[cc]]
    rank_cc <- display_selection$distance_rank[match(cc, display_selection$cntry)]

    png(file.path(
          FIGURE_DIR,
          paste0(sprintf("rank_%02d_", rank_cc), "network_R9_R10_diff_", cc, ".png")
        ),
        width = 15, height = 5, units = "in", res = 300)
    par(mfrow = c(1, 3))
    qgraph(W9, layout = common_layout_all, labels = paste0("V", seq_along(bhv)),
           posCol = "blue", negCol = "red", maximum = global_maximum_all,
           title = paste0(cc, " R9 | distance rank ", rank_cc))
    qgraph(W10, layout = common_layout_all, labels = paste0("V", seq_along(bhv)),
           posCol = "blue", negCol = "red", maximum = global_maximum_all,
           title = paste0(cc, " R10 | distance rank ", rank_cc))
    qgraph(Wdiff, layout = common_layout_all, labels = paste0("V", seq_along(bhv)),
           posCol = "blue", negCol = "red", maximum = global_maximum_all,
           title = paste0(cc, " R10 - R9 | distance rank ", rank_cc))
    dev.off()
  }
}
```

### 6. Accuracy audit for the networks in both rounds

This step is computationally heavy. For a real run, set `RUN_NETWORK_ACCURACY` to `TRUE`.
Both R9 and R10 receive a non-parametric bootstrap of the edge weights and a case-dropping bootstrap for centrality. Centrality is treated as supplementary throughout.

```{r multicountry-network-accuracy}
RUN_NETWORK_ACCURACY <- FALSE
BOOTNET_N             <- 500L
RUN_BOOTNET_SMOKE_TEST <- TRUE
RUN_NETWORK_ACCURACY_EXPORTS <- TRUE
BOOTNET_EQ_TOL         <- 1e-10

## bootnet is given the project's single formal estimation function, rather than relying on the implicit behaviour of default = "mgm".
## That function is called both for the initial estimate by estimateNetwork and for every bootstrap resample, so the bootstrap audits exactly the network that is reported.
bootnet_exact_mgm_fun <- function(data) {
  fitted <- fit_mgm_network(as.matrix(data))
  list(graph = fitted$W, results = fitted$model)
}

estimate_bootnet_exact_mgm <- function(data) {
  estimateNetwork(
    data     = data,
    fun      = bootnet_exact_mgm_fun,
    labels   = bhv,
    weighted = TRUE,
    verbose  = FALSE
  )
}

accuracy_metadata <- list(
  analysis_version = ANALYSIS_VERSION,
  countries        = countries.both,
  nodes            = bhv,
  estimator        = "custom_fun_calls_fit_mgm_network",
  mgm_k            = MGM_K,
  lambda_sel       = MGM_LAMBDA_SEL,
  lambda_gam       = MGM_LAMBDA_GAM,
  mgm_rule         = MGM_RULE,
  mgm_threshold    = MGM_THRESHOLD,
  mgm_scale        = MGM_SCALE,
  mgm_binary_sign  = MGM_BINARY_SIGN,
  n_boots          = BOOTNET_N,
  waves            = c("R9", "R10"),
  data_signature   = data_signature,
  bootnet_version  = as.character(packageVersion("bootnet"))
)

ACCURACY_FILE <- file.path(RESULT_DIR, paste0("network_accuracy_b", BOOTNET_N, ".rds"))

if (file.exists(ACCURACY_FILE)) {
  accuracy_cache <- readRDS(ACCURACY_FILE)
  if (!identical(accuracy_cache$metadata, accuracy_metadata)) {
    warning("The accuracy cache does not match the current data or parameters and has been reset.")
    accuracy_cache <- list(metadata = accuracy_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
  }
} else {
  accuracy_cache <- list(metadata = accuracy_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
}

## A smoke test that gates the full run: first confirm that the same country's R10 network comes out identical through both entry points,
## then actually complete two non-parametric bootstraps. If either step fails, the script stops before the full switch is turned on.
run_bootnet_smoke_test <- function(cc = countries.both[1], wave = "R10") {
  data <- if (wave == "R9") d9[[cc]] else d10[[cc]]
  main_W <- signed_networks_all[[cc]][[wave]]
  bootnet_estimated <- estimate_bootnet_exact_mgm(data)
  bootnet_W <- bootnet_estimated$graph

  if (!all(dim(bootnet_W) == dim(main_W))) {
    stop("The bootnet smoke test failed: network dimensions differ from the formal network.", call. = FALSE)
  }

  max_abs_difference <- max(abs(unname(bootnet_W) - unname(main_W)))
  if (!is.finite(max_abs_difference) || max_abs_difference > BOOTNET_EQ_TOL) {
    stop(paste0(
      "The bootnet smoke test failed: max(abs(W_bootnet - W_main)) = ",
      signif(max_abs_difference, 6),
      ", exceeding the tolerance of ", BOOTNET_EQ_TOL
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }

  smoke_boot <- bootnet(
    bootnet_estimated,
    nBoots    = 2L,
    type      = "nonparametric",
    statistics = "edge",
    nCores    = 1L,
    verbose   = FALSE
  )

  list(
    summary = tibble(
      cntry = cc,
      wave = wave,
      max_abs_difference = max_abs_difference,
      tolerance = BOOTNET_EQ_TOL,
      bootstrap_replicates_completed = 2L
    ),
    estimated = bootnet_estimated,
    smoke_boot = smoke_boot
  )
}

if (RUN_BOOTNET_SMOKE_TEST) {
  set.seed(NETWORK_SEED_BASE + 999L)
  bootnet_smoke_test <- run_bootnet_smoke_test(countries.both[1], "R10")
  print(bootnet_smoke_test$summary)
  write.csv(bootnet_smoke_test$summary,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "bootnet_estimator_smoke_test.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
}

run_accuracy_wave <- function(data) {
  estimated <- estimate_bootnet_exact_mgm(data)

  list(
    estimated_network = estimated,
    edge_accuracy = bootnet(
      estimated,
      nBoots = BOOTNET_N,
      type = "nonparametric",
      statistics = "edge",
      nCores = 1L,
      verbose = FALSE
    ),
    centrality_stability = bootnet(
      estimated,
      nBoots = BOOTNET_N,
      type = "case",
      statistics = c("strength", "expectedInfluence"),
      nCores = 1L,
      verbose = FALSE
    )
  )
}

if (RUN_NETWORK_ACCURACY) {
  for (cc in countries.both) {
    if (!is.null(accuracy_cache$results[[cc]])) next

    message("Two-wave network accuracy audit: ", cc)
    set.seed(NETWORK_SEED_BASE + 1000L + match(cc, countries.both))

    one_accuracy <- tryCatch(
      list(R9 = run_accuracy_wave(d9[[cc]]),
           R10 = run_accuracy_wave(d10[[cc]])),
      error = function(e) structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)), class = "accuracy_error")
    )

    if (inherits(one_accuracy, "accuracy_error")) {
      accuracy_cache$errors[[cc]] <- one_accuracy$message
    } else {
      accuracy_cache$results[[cc]] <- one_accuracy
      accuracy_cache$errors[[cc]] <- NULL
    }
    saveRDS(accuracy_cache, ACCURACY_FILE)
  }
}

extract_cs <- function(boot_object, statistic_pattern) {
  cs <- corStability(boot_object)
  hit <- grep(statistic_pattern, names(cs), ignore.case = TRUE)
  if (length(hit) == 0L) return(NA_real_)
  as.numeric(cs[hit[1]])
}

accuracy_completed <- intersect(countries.both, names(accuracy_cache$results))
if (length(accuracy_completed) > 0L) {
  accuracy_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(accuracy_completed, function(cc) {
    r <- accuracy_cache$results[[cc]]
    bind_rows(lapply(c("R9", "R10"), function(wave) {
      tibble(
        cntry = cc,
        wave = wave,
        cs_strength = extract_cs(r[[wave]]$centrality_stability, "strength"),
        cs_expected_influence = extract_cs(
          r[[wave]]$centrality_stability, "expected.*influence|expectedInfluence"
        )
      )
    }))
  }))

  write.csv(accuracy_summary,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "network_accuracy_summary_two_waves.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
}

## ---- 6.1 Bootstrap quantile intervals for all 210 edges, both rounds, all 20 countries -------------------
ACCURACY_COMPLETE <- setequal(accuracy_completed, countries.both)

extract_edge_accuracy_table <- function(cc, wave) {
  edge_boot <- accuracy_cache$results[[cc]][[wave]]$edge_accuracy
  edge_summary <- summary(edge_boot, statistics = "edge") %>%
    ungroup()

  required_columns <- c(
    "node1", "node2", "sample", "mean", "sd", "q2.5", "q97.5", "prop0"
  )
  missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(edge_summary))
  if (length(missing_columns) > 0L) {
    stop(paste0(
      "The edge-accuracy summary for ", cc, " ", wave,
      " is missing columns: ", paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }

  item1 <- as.character(edge_summary$node1)
  item2 <- as.character(edge_summary$node2)
  i <- match(item1, bhv)
  j <- match(item2, bhv)

  if (anyNA(i) || anyNA(j)) {
    stop(paste0(
      "The edge-accuracy node names for ", cc, " ", wave,
      " cannot be matched to the bhv node order."
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }

  pair_id <- paste(pmin(i, j), pmax(i, j), sep = "--")
  if (nrow(edge_summary) != choose(length(bhv), 2L) ||
      n_distinct(pair_id) != choose(length(bhv), 2L)) {
    stop(paste0(
      "The edge-accuracy summary for ", cc, " ", wave,
      " does not contain exactly 210 unique unordered edges."
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }

  formal_W <- signed_networks_all[[cc]][[wave]]
  formal_edge <- formal_W[cbind(i, j)]
  if (max(abs(as.numeric(edge_summary$sample) - formal_edge)) > BOOTNET_EQ_TOL) {
    stop(paste0(
      "The edge-accuracy sample estimates for ", cc, " ", wave,
      " do not reproduce the formal signed network."
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }

  tibble(
    cntry = cc,
    wave = wave,
    node1 = paste0("V", i),
    node2 = paste0("V", j),
    item1 = item1,
    item2 = item2,
    sample_edge = as.numeric(edge_summary$sample),
    bootstrap_mean = as.numeric(edge_summary$mean),
    bootstrap_sd = as.numeric(edge_summary$sd),
    ci_lower_2.5 = as.numeric(edge_summary[["q2.5"]]),
    ci_upper_97.5 = as.numeric(edge_summary[["q97.5"]]),
    ci_includes_zero = ci_lower_2.5 <= 0 & ci_upper_97.5 >= 0,
    bootstrap_zero_proportion = as.numeric(edge_summary$prop0)
  )
}

if (RUN_NETWORK_ACCURACY_EXPORTS && ACCURACY_COMPLETE) {
  accuracy_edges_all <- bind_rows(lapply(countries.both, function(cc) {
    bind_rows(lapply(c("R9", "R10"), function(wave) {
      extract_edge_accuracy_table(cc, wave)
    }))
  })) %>%
    arrange(match(cntry, countries.both), wave, node1, node2)

  expected_edge_rows <- length(countries.both) * 2L * choose(length(bhv), 2L)
  numeric_accuracy_columns <- c(
    "sample_edge", "bootstrap_mean", "bootstrap_sd",
    "ci_lower_2.5", "ci_upper_97.5", "bootstrap_zero_proportion"
  )

  if (nrow(accuracy_edges_all) != expected_edge_rows) {
    stop(paste0(
      "The final edge-accuracy table has ", nrow(accuracy_edges_all),
      " rows instead of the required ", expected_edge_rows, "."
    ), call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (any(!vapply(accuracy_edges_all[numeric_accuracy_columns], is.numeric, logical(1))) ||
      any(!is.finite(as.matrix(accuracy_edges_all[numeric_accuracy_columns])))) {
    stop("The final edge-accuracy table contains non-numeric or non-finite audit values.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (any(accuracy_edges_all$ci_lower_2.5 > accuracy_edges_all$ci_upper_97.5)) {
    stop("At least one bootstrap quantile interval has its lower bound above its upper bound.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }
  if (any(accuracy_edges_all$bootstrap_zero_proportion < 0 |
          accuracy_edges_all$bootstrap_zero_proportion > 1)) {
    stop("At least one bootstrap zero proportion lies outside [0, 1].",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  ACCURACY_EDGE_CSV <- file.path(
    RESULT_DIR,
    paste0("network_accuracy_edges_all20_two_waves_b", BOOTNET_N, ".csv")
  )
  write.csv(accuracy_edges_all, ACCURACY_EDGE_CSV, row.names = FALSE)

  ## ---- 6.2 One standard bootnet edge-accuracy plot per country and round -----------------------
  ACCURACY_PLOT_DIR <- file.path(
    RESULT_DIR,
    paste0("network_accuracy_edge_plots_b", BOOTNET_N)
  )
  dir.create(ACCURACY_PLOT_DIR, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

  expected_plot_files <- character()
  for (cc in countries.both) {
    for (wave in c("R9", "R10")) {
      edge_boot <- accuracy_cache$results[[cc]][[wave]]$edge_accuracy
      edge_plot <- plot(
        edge_boot,
        statistics = "edge",
        CIstyle = "quantiles",
        alpha = 0.05,
        order = "sample",
        labels = FALSE,
        onlyNonZero = FALSE,
        verbose = FALSE
      ) +
        ggtitle(paste0(cc, " ", wave, " edge-weight accuracy (", BOOTNET_N,
                       " nonparametric bootstraps)"))

      plot_file <- file.path(
        ACCURACY_PLOT_DIR,
        paste0("edge_accuracy_", cc, "_", wave, "_b", BOOTNET_N, ".png")
      )
      expected_plot_files <- c(expected_plot_files, plot_file)

      ggsave(
        filename = plot_file,
        plot = edge_plot,
        width = 10,
        height = 12,
        units = "in",
        dpi = 300,
        bg = "white",
        limitsize = FALSE
      )
    }
  }

  if (length(expected_plot_files) != length(countries.both) * 2L ||
      any(!file.exists(expected_plot_files))) {
    stop("The batch edge-accuracy export did not produce all 40 expected PNG files.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  message(
    "Network-accuracy export complete: ", nrow(accuracy_edges_all),
    " edge rows and ", length(expected_plot_files), " PNG files."
  )
} else if (RUN_NETWORK_ACCURACY_EXPORTS) {
  message(
    "Network accuracy has not yet covered all 20 countries: completed ",
    length(accuracy_completed),
    "/20. No final 8,400-row edge CSV or 40-plot batch was generated."
  )
}
```

### 7. Exploratory community analysis

This section uses the glasso network of EGA, which is not the same model as the main MGM network. It serves as supplementary description only,
and it blocks nothing: the 40 main networks, the 20-country NCT and the cross-country synthesis do not depend on it. For a real run, set `RUN_COMMUNITY_ANALYSIS` to `TRUE`.

```{r multicountry-community-exploratory}
## EGA and bootEGA for all 20 countries were completed on 2026-08-27 and written to the cache, so this switch stays FALSE.
## The summary and export code sits outside the if block and still reads the cache and regenerates the CSV files, without re-running any bootEGA.
## Set it back to TRUE only to recompute the community analysis itself (20 countries by 1000 bootEGA replications takes hours).
RUN_COMMUNITY_ANALYSIS <- FALSE
BOOT_EGA_ITER           <- 1000L

adjusted_rand_index <- function(x, y) {
  tab <- table(x, y)
  choose2 <- function(z) z * (z - 1) / 2
  n <- sum(tab)
  if (n < 2L) return(NA_real_)

  sum_cells <- sum(choose2(tab))
  sum_rows  <- sum(choose2(rowSums(tab)))
  sum_cols  <- sum(choose2(colSums(tab)))
  expected  <- sum_rows * sum_cols / choose2(n)
  maximum   <- 0.5 * (sum_rows + sum_cols)
  denom     <- maximum - expected

  if (abs(denom) < .Machine$double.eps) {
    return(ifelse(identical(as.integer(x), as.integer(y)), 1, NA_real_))
  }
  (sum_cells - expected) / denom
}

community_metadata <- list(
  analysis_version = ANALYSIS_VERSION,
  countries        = countries.both,
  nodes            = bhv,
  model            = "glasso",
  algorithm        = "walktrap_default",
  boot_iterations  = BOOT_EGA_ITER,
  data_signature   = data_signature,
  eganet_version   = as.character(packageVersion("EGAnet"))
)

COMMUNITY_FILE <- file.path(
  RESULT_DIR, paste0("community_exploratory_boot", BOOT_EGA_ITER, ".rds")
)

if (file.exists(COMMUNITY_FILE)) {
  community_cache <- readRDS(COMMUNITY_FILE)
  if (!identical(community_cache$metadata, community_metadata)) {
    warning("The community-analysis cache does not match the current data or parameters and has been reset.")
    community_cache <- list(metadata = community_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
  }
} else {
  community_cache <- list(metadata = community_metadata, results = list(), errors = list())
}

if (RUN_COMMUNITY_ANALYSIS) {
  for (cc in countries.both) {
    if (!is.null(community_cache$results[[cc]])) next

    message("Exploratory community analysis: ", cc)
    set.seed(NETWORK_SEED_BASE + 2000L + match(cc, countries.both))

    one_community <- tryCatch({
      ega9  <- EGA(d9[[cc]],  model = "glasso", plot.EGA = FALSE)
      ega10 <- EGA(d10[[cc]], model = "glasso", plot.EGA = FALSE)
      bega9  <- bootEGA(d9[[cc]],  iter = BOOT_EGA_ITER, model = "glasso")
      bega10 <- bootEGA(d10[[cc]], iter = BOOT_EGA_ITER, model = "glasso")

      list(
        EGA_R9 = ega9,
        EGA_R10 = ega10,
        bootEGA_R9 = bega9,
        bootEGA_R10 = bega10,
        item_stability_R9 = itemStability(bega9),
        item_stability_R10 = itemStability(bega10),
        ari_R9_R10 = adjusted_rand_index(ega9$wc, ega10$wc)
      )
    }, error = function(e) {
      structure(list(message = conditionMessage(e)), class = "community_error")
    })

    if (inherits(one_community, "community_error")) {
      community_cache$errors[[cc]] <- one_community$message
    } else {
      community_cache$results[[cc]] <- one_community
      community_cache$errors[[cc]] <- NULL
    }
    saveRDS(community_cache, COMMUNITY_FILE)
  }
}

community_completed <- intersect(countries.both, names(community_cache$results))
if (length(community_completed) > 0L) {
  ## Correction made on 2026-09-06: EGA can leave an item on a community boundary unassigned as NA (iprspot in Portugal R10 is the only such case),
  ## and unique() keeps NA as one of its values by default, which inflated the community count for such a country by one.
  ## na.omit() must come before counting. The number of unassigned items and the number of items actually used for the ARI are exported as well, so this cannot go unnoticed again.
  community_summary <- bind_rows(lapply(community_completed, function(cc) {
    r   <- community_cache$results[[cc]]
    w9  <- r$EGA_R9$wc
    w10 <- r$EGA_R10$wc
    tibble(
      cntry = cc,
      n_communities_R9  = length(unique(na.omit(w9))),
      n_communities_R10 = length(unique(na.omit(w10))),
      n_unassigned_R9   = sum(is.na(w9)),
      n_unassigned_R10  = sum(is.na(w10)),
      ## The table() call inside adjusted_rand_index() silently drops any pair containing NA.
      ## This column records how many items each country's ARI is actually based on, so the basis can be stated in the report.
      n_items_used_in_ari = sum(!is.na(w9) & !is.na(w10)),
      ari_R9_R10 = r$ari_R9_R10,
      median_item_stability_R9 =
        median(r$item_stability_R9$item.stability$empirical.dimensions, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_item_stability_R10 =
        median(r$item_stability_R10$item.stability$empirical.dimensions, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  }))

  write.csv(community_summary,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "community_summary_exploratory.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)

  ## Per-item community stability for all 40 networks (the table required by Section 6.8 of the project outline)
  MAX_DIM <- 7L
  item_stability_all <- bind_rows(lapply(community_completed, function(cc) {
    bind_rows(lapply(c("R9", "R10"), function(w) {
      is_obj <- community_cache$results[[cc]][[paste0("item_stability_", w)]]
      ega    <- community_cache$results[[cc]][[paste0("EGA_", w)]]
      ed     <- is_obj$item.stability$empirical.dimensions
      ad     <- is_obj$item.stability$all.dimensions
      bm     <- is_obj$membership$bootstrap

      props <- matrix(NA_real_, nrow = length(bhv), ncol = MAX_DIM)
      props[, seq_len(ncol(ad))] <- ad
      colnames(props) <- paste0("prop_dim", seq_len(MAX_DIM))

      bind_cols(
        tibble(
          cntry = cc,
          wave  = w,
          node  = paste0("V", seq_along(bhv)),
          item  = bhv,
          empirical_community     = as.integer(ega$wc),
          is_unassigned           = is.na(ega$wc),
          item_stability          = as.numeric(ed),
          prop_unassigned_in_boot = as.numeric(colMeans(is.na(bm))),
          modal_boot_community    = as.integer(apply(ad, 1, which.max)),
          modal_boot_proportion   = as.numeric(apply(ad, 1, max)),
          n_communities_empirical = length(unique(na.omit(ega$wc)))
        ),
        as_tibble(props)
      )
    }))
  }))

  if (nrow(item_stability_all) != length(community_completed) * 2L * length(bhv)) {
    stop("The per-item community stability table does not have 20 countries x 2 waves x 21 items.",
         call. = FALSE)
  }

  write.csv(item_stability_all,
            file.path(RESULT_DIR, "community_item_stability_all40.csv"),
            row.names = FALSE)
}
```


# Part 2. Verification of the reported results, and the figures

The chunks below correspond one to one with the sections of the Results chapter, recomputing and printing every number reported there.
This part reads only the CSV files written by Part 1 and the raw data. It re-estimates no network and re-runs no permutation test or bootstrap.
The descriptive statistics need individual-level data, so the first chunk rebuilds an analysis sample equivalent to the one used in the formal analysis,
and then checks that the 40 country-by-round sample sizes it produces match the formal networks exactly. A reviewer can therefore treat this part as an independent recomputation.


```{r report-setup}
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(psych)    # skew() / kurtosi(); type = 2 matches the bias-corrected formula used by pandas
library(ggplot2)

## ---- Paths -----------------------------------------------------------------
## RES holds everything Part 1 wrote and is all that is needed to reproduce the results.
## ALT is a legacy folder from the working project that holds copies of a few of the same files. The copies are byte-identical to those in RES,
## so RES is always searched first and ALT is never reached when the supplementary materials are used as distributed. Its absence is expected and is handled.
ROOT <- "."
RES  <- file.path(ROOT, "multicountry_results", "mgm_multicountry_v3")
ALT  <- file.path(ROOT, "20国统计")   # legacy fallback folder in the working project; not required, and absent from the distributed materials
OUT  <- file.path(ROOT, "results_tables")
dir.create(OUT, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## Look in RES first, then in ALT. Files of the same name in the two folders have identical contents.
find_csv <- function(fname) {
  for (d in c(RES, ALT)) {
    p <- file.path(d, fname)
    if (file.exists(p)) return(p)
  }
    stop("Result file not found: ", fname, call. = FALSE)
}

## ---- Constants ---------------------------------------------------------------
ITEMS <- c("impdiff","impenv","impfree","impfun","imprich","impsafe","imptrad",
           "ipadvnt","ipbhprp","ipcrtiv","ipeqopt","ipfrule","ipgdtim","iphlppl",
           "iplylfr","ipmodst","iprspot","ipshabt","ipstrgv","ipsuces","ipudrst")
VALID <- 1:6           # valid responses; 7 = refusal, 8 = do not know, 9 = no answer
N_NODES <- length(ITEMS)
N_EDGES <- choose(N_NODES, 2)   # 210

## Item to Schwartz value type and higher-order dimension, used to make the result tables readable. The mapping follows the ESS questionnaire documentation
ITEM_MAP <- tibble::tribble(
  ~item,      ~value_type,      ~higher_order,
  "impdiff",  "Stimulation",    "Openness",
  "impenv",   "Universalism",   "Self-transcendence",

  "ipadvnt",  "Stimulation",    "Openness",
  "ipbhprp",  "Conformity",     "Conservation",
  "ipcrtiv",  "Self-direction", "Openness",
  "ipeqopt",  "Universalism",   "Self-transcendence",
  "ipfrule",  "Conformity",     "Conservation",
  "ipgdtim",  "Hedonism",       "Openness",
  "iphlppl",  "Benevolence",    "Self-transcendence",
  "iplylfr",  "Benevolence",    "Self-transcendence",
  "ipmodst",  "Tradition",      "Conservation",
  "iprspot",  "Power",          "Self-enhancement",
  "ipshabt",  "Achievement",    "Self-enhancement",
  "ipstrgv",  "Security",       "Conservation",
  "ipsuces",  "Achievement",    "Self-enhancement",

) %>% mutate(node = paste0("V", match(item, ITEMS)))

## Short English item labels for the figures. All figures use English labels so that no Chinese font has to be available on the machine that draws them
ITEM_EN <- c(impdiff="try new things", impenv="care for environment",
             impfree="make own decisions", impfun="seek fun", imprich="be rich",
             impsafe="safe surroundings", imptrad="follow traditions",
             ipadvnt="seek adventure", ipbhprp="behave properly",
             ipcrtiv="be creative", ipeqopt="equal opportunities",
             ipfrule="follow rules", ipgdtim="have a good time",
             iphlppl="help people", iplylfr="loyal to friends", ipmodst="be modest",
             iprspot="get respect", ipshabt="show abilities",
             ipstrgv="strong government", ipsuces="be successful",
             ipudrst="understand others")

## Chinese item labels, carried over from the Chinese-language draft of the manuscript. They appear as extra columns in some exported CSV files and are not used anywhere in the submitted report
ITEM_CN <- c(impdiff="尝试新鲜事物", impenv="关心环境", impfree="自己做决定",
             impfun="寻求乐趣", imprich="富有", impsafe="生活安全", imptrad="遵循传统",
             ipadvnt="寻求冒险", ipbhprp="举止得体", ipcrtiv="有创造力",
             ipeqopt="人人平等", ipfrule="遵守规则", ipgdtim="享受美好时光",
             iphlppl="帮助他人", iplylfr="忠于朋友", ipmodst="谦逊低调",
             iprspot="获得尊重", ipshabt="展示才能", ipstrgv="政府保障安全",
             ipsuces="取得成功", ipudrst="理解他人")

## Items ordered by motivational position on the Schwartz circle, so that the theoretical blocks are visible in the figures
CIRCLE_ORDER <- c("ipcrtiv","impfree",              # Self-direction
                  "impdiff","ipadvnt",              # Stimulation
                  "ipgdtim","impfun",               # Hedonism
                  "ipshabt","ipsuces",              # Achievement
                  "imprich","iprspot",              # Power
                  "impsafe","ipstrgv",              # Security
                  "ipfrule","ipbhprp",              # Conformity
                  "ipmodst","imptrad",              # Tradition
                  "iphlppl","iplylfr",              # Benevolence
                  "ipudrst","ipeqopt","impenv")     # Universalism
stopifnot(setequal(CIRCLE_ORDER, ITEMS))
ITEM_MAP <- ITEM_MAP %>%
  mutate(item_cn = unname(ITEM_CN[item]),
         item_en = unname(ITEM_EN[item]),
         circle_pos = match(item, CIRCLE_ORDER),
         higher_order_cn = recode(higher_order,
           "Openness" = "开放改变", "Self-enhancement" = "自我提升",
           "Conservation" = "保守", "Self-transcendence" = "自我超越"))

show <- function(label, ...) cat(sprintf("[%s] ", label), ..., "\n", sep = "")

## ---- Plotting setup ----------------------------------------------------------
FIG <- file.path(ROOT, "results_figures")
dir.create(FIG, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)

## Palette: blue and orange for the two rounds, a blue/red diverging pair for direction of change, neutral grey for secondary objects.
## All three pairings were checked against colour-vision-deficiency simulation, and the worst pairing is well above the threshold for discriminability.
BLUE <- "#2a78d6"; ORANGE <- "#eb6834"; RED <- "#e34948"; GREY <- "#6f6e6a"

theme_thesis <- theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major.x = element_line(colour = "grey88", linewidth = 0.3),
        axis.title = element_text(colour = "#52514e"),
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 12),
        plot.subtitle = element_text(colour = "#52514e", size = 9),
        plot.caption = element_text(colour = "#52514e", size = 8, hjust = 0),
        legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank())

## The default ggsave device (ragg) fails to write a file on some systems, so the base png device is used as a fallback.
## The old file is deleted first: otherwise file.exists() would still be TRUE after a failed write, the fallback branch would not trigger,
## and a re-run would silently leave the previous version of the figure in place.
save_fig <- function(file, plot, width = 7, height = 6, dpi = 300) {
  if (file.exists(file)) unlink(file)
  ok <- tryCatch({
    suppressWarnings(ggsave(file, plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi, bg = "white"))
    file.exists(file)
  }, error = function(e) FALSE)
  if (!ok) {
    ggsave(file, plot, width = width, height = height, dpi = dpi, bg = "white",
           device = grDevices::png, type = "cairo")
  }
  invisible(file.exists(file))
}
```

## 1. Descriptive statistics

## 1.0 Rebuilding the analysis sample (not a reported result)

This chunk rebuilds a sample equivalent to the one used in Part 1, for use by the descriptive statistics that follow.
The order of operations matches Part 1: values outside 1-6 on the 21 items are set to `NA`, cases with any missing item are dropped, and the items are then reverse coded.
The chunk ends by checking that the rebuilt sample reproduces the 40 country-by-round sample sizes of the formal networks exactly. If it did not, nothing below could be trusted.

```{r desc-prepare}
raw <- read.csv(file.path(ROOT, "ESS9e03_2-ESS10-subset.csv"))
stopifnot(length(ITEMS) == 21, all(ITEMS %in% names(raw)))

df <- raw %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ITEMS), ~ ifelse(.x %in% VALID, .x, NA_integer_))) %>%
  drop_na(all_of(ITEMS)) %>%
  mutate(across(all_of(ITEMS), ~ 7L - .x))
stopifnot(all(unlist(df[ITEMS]) %in% VALID))

both20 <- df %>% distinct(cntry, essround) %>% count(cntry) %>%
  filter(n == 2) %>% pull(cntry) %>% sort()
sub <- df %>% filter(cntry %in% both20)

## Check: the 40 country-by-round sample sizes must match the formal networks exactly
dg_check <- read.csv(find_csv("network_diagnostics_40.csv"))
cmp <- dg_check %>%
  select(cntry, wave, n_network = n) %>%
  left_join(sub %>% count(cntry, essround) %>%
              mutate(wave = ifelse(essround == 9, "R9", "R10")) %>%
              select(cntry, wave, n_reproduced = n),
            by = c("cntry", "wave"))
show("40 country-by-round sample sizes match the formal networks", all(cmp$n_network == cmp$n_reproduced))
show("Largest absolute difference", max(abs(cmp$n_network - cmp$n_reproduced)))
```

## 1.1 The analysis sample

```{r desc-sample}
show("Countries included", length(both20))
show("Country list", paste(both20, collapse = ", "))
show("Complete respondents", "R9 ", sum(sub$essround == 9),
     ", R10 ", sum(sub$essround == 10), ", total ", nrow(sub))

tabA <- sub %>%
  count(cntry, essround, name = "n") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = essround, values_from = n, names_prefix = "n_R") %>%
  mutate(ratio = n_R10 / n_R9) %>%
  arrange(cntry)
print(as.data.frame(tabA), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
write.csv(tabA, file.path(OUT, "tableA_sample_sizes.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

show("Range of single-round sample sizes", min(c(tabA$n_R9, tabA$n_R10)), " (",
     tabA$cntry[which.min(pmin(tabA$n_R9, tabA$n_R10))], " R9) – ",
     max(c(tabA$n_R9, tabA$n_R10)), " (",
     tabA$cntry[which.max(pmax(tabA$n_R9, tabA$n_R10))], " R10)")
show("Countries whose two rounds differ most in size (ratio below 0.7 or above 1.4)",
     paste(sprintf("%s %.2f", tabA$cntry[tabA$ratio < 0.7 | tabA$ratio > 1.4],
                   tabA$ratio[tabA$ratio < 0.7 | tabA$ratio > 1.4]), collapse = "; "))
```

## 1.2 Distribution of the 21 value items

```{r desc-items}
tabC <- sub %>%
  select(essround, all_of(ITEMS)) %>%

            floor_pct = 100 * mean(v == 1), ceiling_pct = 100 * mean(v == 6),

  left_join(ITEM_MAP, by = "item") %>%
  mutate(item = factor(item, levels = ITEMS)) %>%

print(as.data.frame(tabC %>% select(node, item, value_type, essround, mean, sd,

write.csv(tabC, file.path(OUT, "tableC_item_descriptives.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

show("Range of item means", sprintf("%.2f - %.2f (highest %s, lowest %s)",

show("Range of item standard deviations", sprintf("%.2f - %.2f", min(tabC$sd), max(tabC$sd)))
show("Range of skewness", sprintf("%.3f - %.3f", min(tabC$skew), max(tabC$skew)))
show("Range of excess kurtosis", sprintf("%.3f - %.3f", min(tabC$kurtosis), max(tabC$kurtosis)))
show("Item-by-round cells with |skew| > 1", sum(abs(tabC$skew) > 1), " / ", nrow(tabC),
     "; items involved: ", paste(unique(as.character(tabC$item[abs(tabC$skew) > 1])), collapse = ", "))
show("Cells with |kurtosis| > 7", sum(abs(tabC$kurtosis) > 7))

## Ceiling and floor effects, averaged over the two rounds

  summarise(ceiling_pct = mean(ceiling_pct), floor_pct = mean(floor_pct), .groups = "drop")
show("Items with a ceiling above 25%",
```
