
Figure 1 shows the full response distribution of the 21 items in both rounds.

One choice of plot needs explaining. Box plots were used at first, but they carry very little information on a six-point scale:
across the 42 item-by-round combinations the interquartile range takes only 5 distinct (Q1, Q3) combinations,
so most items plot on top of one another. The reason is that quantiles of discrete data necessarily fall on integers.
With only 6 possible values and more than thirty thousand respondents per round, the two adjacent order statistics that define the
25th, 50th and 75th percentiles are almost always equal, so linear interpolation returns that integer. The code below checks this explicitly,
to make clear that the data themselves were never rounded. A heat map of response proportions by category is used instead:
it keeps the full distribution of each item over the 6 options and makes the two rounds easy to compare side by side.

```{r fig-item-distribution, fig.width=10, fig.height=8}
## Check: the data are integers, and quantiles landing on integers is an inevitable property of a discrete scale rather than the result of any rounding
stopifnot(all(unlist(sub[ITEMS]) %in% VALID))
qs <- sub %>% select(essround, all_of(ITEMS)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(ITEMS), names_to = "item", values_to = "v") %>%
  group_by(item, essround) %>%
  summarise(q1 = quantile(v, .25), med = median(v), q3 = quantile(v, .75), .groups = "drop")
show("Non-integer quantiles among the 42 item-by-round cells",
     sum(c(qs$q1, qs$med, qs$q3) != round(c(qs$q1, qs$med, qs$q3))), " / ", 3 * nrow(qs))
show("Distinct (Q1, Q3) combinations", nrow(distinct(qs, q1, q3)), " (this is why the box plots were so repetitive)")

## Response proportions by category
dist_dat <- sub %>%
  select(essround, all_of(ITEMS)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(ITEMS), names_to = "item", values_to = "v") %>%
  count(essround, item, v) %>%
  group_by(essround, item) %>%
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  left_join(ITEM_MAP, by = "item") %>%
  mutate(wave = factor(ifelse(essround == 9, "Round 9", "Round 10"),
                       levels = c("Round 9", "Round 10")))

## Ordered by the mean over both rounds, so items answered more towards "like me" sit at the top
item_order <- sub %>% select(all_of(ITEMS)) %>%
  summarise(across(everything(), mean)) %>%
  pivot_longer(everything(), names_to = "item", values_to = "m") %>%
  arrange(m) %>% pull(item)
dist_dat <- dist_dat %>%
  mutate(label = factor(sprintf("%s  (%s)", item, item_en),
                        levels = sprintf("%s  (%s)", item_order,
                                         ITEM_EN[item_order])))

p_dist <- ggplot(dist_dat, aes(x = factor(v), y = label, fill = pct)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "white", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.0f", pct),
                colour = pct > 22), size = 2.6, show.legend = FALSE) +
  facet_wrap(~ wave) +
  ## Sequential scale for a continuous quantity: a single blue from light to dark, with the light end meaning a proportion near zero
  scale_fill_gradient(low = "#eaf2fd", high = "#0d366b", name = "% of\nrespondents") +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "#0b0b0b", `TRUE` = "white")) +
  labs(title = "Figure 1. Response distribution of the 21 value items, by round",
       subtitle = "Cell values are the percentage of respondents choosing each option (rows sum to 100)",
       x = "Response  (1 = not like me at all  ...  6 = very much like me)", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Pooled 20-country sample (R9 n = 31,687; R10 n = 31,068). ",
                        "Items ordered by overall mean, lowest at the bottom.\n",
                        "The formal round comparison, with survey weights and multiplicity correction, is reported in 3.1.")) +
  theme_thesis +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
        legend.position = "right", legend.title = element_text(colour = "#52514e", size = 8))
save_fig(file.path(FIG, "fig_item_distribution.png"), p_dist, width = 10, height = 8)
p_dist

## Distribution features quoted in the report
mode_tab <- dist_dat %>% group_by(essround, item) %>% slice_max(pct, n = 1) %>% ungroup()
show("Items whose modal response is 5", "R9 ", sum(mode_tab$v[mode_tab$essround == 9] == 5),
     " / 21; R10 ", sum(mode_tab$v[mode_tab$essround == 10] == 5), " / 21")
show("Items whose modal response is 2",
     paste(unique(mode_tab$item[mode_tab$v == 2]), collapse = ", "))

top56 <- dist_dat %>% filter(v >= 5) %>% group_by(essround, item) %>%
  summarise(p56 = sum(pct), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = essround, values_from = p56, names_prefix = "R")
print(as.data.frame(top56 %>% arrange(desc(R9)) %>% head(5)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

cell <- dist_dat %>% select(essround, item, v, pct) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = essround, values_from = pct, names_prefix = "R") %>%
  mutate(diff = abs(R10 - R9))
show("Round difference across the 126 cells", sprintf("median %.2f, %.0f%% within 2 percentage points, maximum %.2f",
     median(cell$diff), 100 * mean(cell$diff <= 2), max(cell$diff)))
print(as.data.frame(cell %>% slice_max(diff, n = 3)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
```

## 1.3 Item mean differences between the two rounds

This section computes effect sizes only, to show how large the mean differences between rounds are.
It is UNWEIGHTED and descriptive. The formal, survey-weighted significance test is in Section 3.1, and it is the one reported in the project report. The two therefore differ slightly, and Section 3.1 is the authoritative figure.

```{r desc-change}
tabD <- sub %>%
  select(essround, all_of(ITEMS)) %>%
  pivot_longer(all_of(ITEMS), names_to = "item", values_to = "v") %>%
  group_by(item, essround) %>%
  summarise(n = n(), m = mean(v), s2 = var(v), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = essround, values_from = c(n, m, s2)) %>%
  mutate(diff = m_10 - m_9,
         s_pooled = sqrt(((n_9 - 1) * s2_9 + (n_10 - 1) * s2_10) / (n_9 + n_10 - 2)),
         cohens_d = diff / s_pooled) %>%
  left_join(ITEM_MAP, by = "item") %>%
  arrange(desc(abs(cohens_d)))
print(as.data.frame(tabD %>% select(node, item, value_type, m_9, m_10, diff, cohens_d)),
      row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
write.csv(tabD, file.path(OUT, "tableD_round_difference.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

show("Largest |d|", sprintf("%.3f (%s)", max(abs(tabD$cohens_d)),
                         tabD$item[which.max(abs(tabD$cohens_d))]))
show("Items with |d| > 0.1", sum(abs(tabD$cohens_d) > 0.1), " / 21")
show("Items with |d| >= 0.2 (the conventional threshold for a small effect)", sum(abs(tabD$cohens_d) >= 0.2), " / 21")
```

## 1.4 Correlations among the items

The mapping of items onto the ten Schwartz basic values and the four higher-order values is given in the Methods chapter.
What follows simply exports a machine-readable version of it, used for the grouped statistics and the figure ordering in this section.

```{r item-mapping}
map_tab <- ITEM_MAP %>%
  arrange(circle_pos) %>%
  select(node, item, item_en, item_cn, value_type, higher_order, higher_order_cn)
print(as.data.frame(map_tab), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(map_tab, file.path(OUT, "table_item_value_mapping.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

show("Number of items per basic value",
     paste(sprintf("%s=%d", names(table(ITEM_MAP$value_type)),
                   as.vector(table(ITEM_MAP$value_type))), collapse = ", "))
show("Number of items per higher-order value",
     paste(sprintf("%s=%d", names(table(ITEM_MAP$higher_order)),
                   as.vector(table(ITEM_MAP$higher_order))), collapse = ", "))
```

```{r desc-cor}
for (rd in c(9, 10)) {
  C  <- cor(sub %>% filter(essround == rd) %>% select(all_of(ITEMS)))
  ut <- C[upper.tri(C)]
  ev <- eigen(C, symmetric = TRUE, only.values = TRUE)$values
  cat(sprintf("R%-3d r range %+.3f to %+.3f | mean %.3f | negative %.1f%% | smallest eigenvalue %.4f | condition number %.1f\n",
              rd, min(ut), max(ut), mean(ut), 100 * mean(ut < 0), min(ev), max(ev) / min(ev)))
  idx <- which(upper.tri(C), arr.ind = TRUE)
  top <- order(abs(C[upper.tri(C)]), decreasing = TRUE)[1:4]
  for (k in top) {
    i <- idx[k, 1]; j <- idx[k, 2]
    cat(sprintf("      %-8s - %-8s %+.3f  (%s / %s)\n", ITEMS[i], ITEMS[j], C[i, j],
                ITEM_MAP$value_type[match(ITEMS[i], ITEM_MAP$item)],
                ITEM_MAP$value_type[match(ITEMS[j], ITEM_MAP$item)]))
  }
}
```

Figure 2 draws the correlation matrix of each round as a heat map. The items are again in circle order, so that if the theoretical grouping holds,
darker blocks should appear within each higher-order value.

```{r fig-correlation-matrix, fig.width=11, fig.height=6}
ord <- ITEM_MAP %>% arrange(circle_pos)
cor_long <- bind_rows(lapply(c(9, 10), function(rd) {
  C <- cor(sub %>% filter(essround == rd) %>% select(all_of(ord$item)))
  diag(C) <- NA_real_          # the self-correlation is always 1 and carries no information, so it is left blank
  as.data.frame(as.table(C)) %>%
    setNames(c("x", "y", "r")) %>%
    mutate(wave = ifelse(rd == 9, "Round 9", "Round 10"))
})) %>%
  mutate(wave = factor(wave, levels = c("Round 9", "Round 10")),
         x = factor(x, levels = ord$item),
         y = factor(y, levels = rev(ord$item)))

sep <- which(ord$higher_order_cn[-1] != ord$higher_order_cn[-nrow(ord)]) + 0.5

p_cor <- ggplot(cor_long, aes(x = x, y = y, fill = r)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_vline(xintercept = sep, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = length(ITEMS) - sep + 1, colour = "white", linewidth = 0.6) +
  facet_wrap(~ wave) +
  ## Diverging palette: neutral grey at 0, blue for positive and red for negative correlations, with symmetric limits
  scale_fill_gradient2(low = RED, mid = "#f0efec", high = BLUE, midpoint = 0,
                       limits = c(-0.6, 0.6), na.value = "grey85", name = "r") +
  labs(title = "Figure 2. Item correlation matrices, Round 9 and Round 10",
       subtitle = "Items ordered by the Schwartz motivational circle; white lines separate the four higher-order values",
       x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Pearson correlations on the pooled 20-country sample. Blocks along the diagonal\n",
                        "correspond to items belonging to the same higher-order value. The grey diagonal is the\n",
                        "self-correlation, which is always 1 and is left out.")) +
  theme_thesis +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5, size = 7),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "right",
        legend.title = element_text(colour = "#52514e"))
save_fig(file.path(FIG, "fig_correlation_matrix.png"), p_cor, width = 11, height = 6)
p_cor

## Mean correlation within versus between higher-order values
for (rd in c(9, 10)) {
  C <- cor(sub %>% filter(essround == rd) %>% select(all_of(ITEMS)))
  ho <- ITEM_MAP$higher_order[match(ITEMS, ITEM_MAP$item)]
  vt <- ITEM_MAP$value_type[match(ITEMS, ITEM_MAP$item)]
  ut <- upper.tri(C)
  same_vt <- outer(vt, vt, "==") & ut
  same_ho <- outer(ho, ho, "==") & ut & !same_vt
  diff_ho <- outer(ho, ho, "!=") & ut
  cat(sprintf("R%-3d within basic value %.3f (%d pairs) | within higher-order value, across basic values %.3f (%d pairs) | across higher-order values %.3f (%d pairs)\n",
              rd, mean(C[same_vt]), sum(same_vt), mean(C[same_ho]), sum(same_ho),
              mean(C[diff_ho]), sum(diff_ho)))
}
```

## 2. Objective 1: structure and precision of the 40 formal networks

All networks were estimated in Part 1 (MGM, `k = 2`, `lambdaSel = "EBIC"`,
`lambdaGam = 0.50`, `ruleReg = "AND"`, `threshold = "LW"`, `scale = TRUE`). This section only reads those results back.

## 2.1 Network diagnostics

```{r g1-diagnostics}
dg <- read.csv(find_csv("network_diagnostics_40.csv"))

## The global-properties table is derived here directly from the diagnostics of the 40 networks, rather than trusting a copied file.
## If global_properties_20countries.csv happens to be present, the two are cross-checked. Its absence is expected and harmless.
gp <- dg %>%
  mutate(density = n_edges / N_EDGES) %>%
  select(cntry, wave, n, n_edges, density, global_strength, mean_present_edge) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = wave,
              values_from = c(n, n_edges, density, global_strength, mean_present_edge)) %>%
  mutate(global_strength_diff = global_strength_R10 - global_strength_R9) %>%
  arrange(cntry)

gp_file <- tryCatch(find_csv("global_properties_20countries.csv"), error = function(e) NA_character_)
if (!is.na(gp_file)) {
  ref <- read.csv(gp_file) %>% arrange(cntry)
  num <- intersect(names(ref), names(gp))
  num <- num[sapply(gp[num], is.numeric)]
  show("Largest absolute deviation from the existing global_properties_20countries.csv",
       signif(max(abs(as.matrix(gp[num]) - as.matrix(ref[num]))), 3),
       " (read from ", gp_file, ")")
}

show("Number of networks", nrow(dg), " (20 countries x 2 rounds)")
show("All pass the symmetry, zero-diagonal and finite-value checks",
     all(dg$symmetric & dg$zero_diagonal & dg$all_finite))
show("All networks have 21 nodes", all(dg$n_nodes == 21))
show("Sample size range", min(dg$n), " (", dg$cntry[which.min(dg$n)], " ", dg$wave[which.min(dg$n)],
     ") to ", max(dg$n), " (", dg$cntry[which.max(dg$n)], " ", dg$wave[which.max(dg$n)], ")")
show("Edge count range", min(dg$n_edges), " to ", max(dg$n_edges), " (out of ", N_EDGES, " possible edges)")
show("Positive edges in total", sum(dg$n_positive_edges), ", negative edges in total ", sum(dg$n_negative_edges),
     sprintf(", negative edges are %.1f%% of all estimated edges", 100 * sum(dg$n_negative_edges) / sum(dg$n_edges)))
show("Global strength range", sprintf("%.2f to %.2f", min(dg$global_strength), max(dg$global_strength)))

## Reported separately by round, so that the two rounds are never merged into a single figure
for (w in c("R9", "R10")) {
  x <- dg %>% filter(wave == w)
  cat(sprintf("%-4s edges %d (%s) to %d (%s), median %.0f | density %.3f to %.3f, median %.3f | positive %d, negative %d (negative %.1f%%)\n",
      w, min(x$n_edges), x$cntry[which.min(x$n_edges)], max(x$n_edges), x$cntry[which.max(x$n_edges)],
      median(x$n_edges), min(x$n_edges)/N_EDGES, max(x$n_edges)/N_EDGES, median(x$n_edges)/N_EDGES,
      sum(x$n_positive_edges), sum(x$n_negative_edges),
      100 * sum(x$n_negative_edges) / sum(x$n_edges)))
}
show("Correlation between edge count and sample size", sprintf("R9 %.3f, R10 %.3f",
     cor(dg$n_edges[dg$wave == "R9"], dg$n[dg$wave == "R9"]),
     cor(dg$n_edges[dg$wave == "R10"], dg$n[dg$wave == "R10"])))
show("Negative edges per network, range", min(dg$n_negative_edges), " to ", max(dg$n_negative_edges),
     sprintf("; as a share of that network's edges, %.1f%% to %.1f%%",
             min(100 * dg$n_negative_edges / dg$n_edges),
             max(100 * dg$n_negative_edges / dg$n_edges)))
```

The report uses France to illustrate what positive and negative edges mean. The selection rule is given in Section 3.4: France is the country closest to the median change pattern of the 20.
The figure itself is the existing three-panel file, which is not regenerated here.

```{r fr-example-edges}
acc_fr <- read.csv(find_csv("network_accuracy_edges_all20_two_waves_b500.csv")) %>%
```

## 2.3 Edge-weight precision (500 non-parametric bootstrap replications)

```{r g1-accuracy-edges}
acc <- read.csv(find_csv("network_accuracy_edges_all20_two_waves_b500.csv"))
stopifnot(nrow(acc) == 20 * 2 * N_EDGES)

show("Total edge records", nrow(acc), " (20 countries x 2 rounds x ", N_EDGES, " edges)")
show("Records whose 95% bootstrap interval contains 0", sum(acc$ci_includes_zero),
     sprintf(" (%.1f%%)", 100 * mean(acc$ci_includes_zero)))

nz <- acc %>% filter(sample_edge != 0)
show("Non-zero edges in the formal networks", nrow(nz),
     ", of which the interval excludes 0 for ", sum(!nz$ci_includes_zero),
     sprintf(" (%.1f%%)", 100 * mean(!nz$ci_includes_zero)))
show("Edges shrunk to exactly 0 by regularisation", sum(acc$sample_edge == 0),
     "; do all their intervals contain 0: ", all(acc$ci_includes_zero[acc$sample_edge == 0]))

## How precision varies with sample size: per country and round, the share of non-zero edges whose interval excludes 0
prec_by_net <- nz %>%
  group_by(cntry, wave) %>%
  summarise(n_nonzero = n(), n_ci_excl_0 = sum(!ci_includes_zero),
            pct_ci_excl_0 = 100 * mean(!ci_includes_zero), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(dg %>% select(cntry, wave, n), by = c("cntry", "wave"))
show("Range across networks of the share of intervals excluding 0",
     sprintf("%.1f%% – %.1f%%", min(prec_by_net$pct_ci_excl_0), max(prec_by_net$pct_ci_excl_0)))
show("Correlation of that share with sample size",
     sprintf("r = %.3f", cor(prec_by_net$pct_ci_excl_0, prec_by_net$n)))
write.csv(prec_by_net, file.path(OUT, "table_edge_precision_by_network.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 3. Objective 2: differences in level and differences in structure

## 3.1 Differences in item endorsement levels (survey-weighted)

```{r g2-level}
lv <- read.csv(file.path(ROOT, "level_test_weighted.csv")) %>%
  left_join(ITEM_MAP, by = "item")

show("Items tested", nrow(lv))
show("Items with Holm-adjusted p < .05", sum(lv$p_holm < .05),
     " (of which d > 0 for ", sum(lv$p_holm < .05 & lv$d > 0),
     " items and d < 0 for ", sum(lv$p_holm < .05 & lv$d < 0), ")")
show("Items with Bonferroni-adjusted p < .05", sum(lv$p_bonf < .05))
show("Largest standardised difference", sprintf("%s, d = %.3f, 95%% CI [%.3f, %.3f]",
     lv$item[which.max(abs(lv$d))], lv$d[which.max(abs(lv$d))],
     lv$d_lo[which.max(abs(lv$d))], lv$d_hi[which.max(abs(lv$d))]))

sig <- lv %>% filter(p_holm < .05) %>% arrange(desc(abs(d)))
show("Range of |d| among the significant items", sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", min(abs(sig$d)), max(abs(sig$d))))
show("Items with |d| >= 0.2 among all 21", sum(abs(lv$d) >= 0.2))

cat("\n-- Significant items, by descending |d| --\n")

      row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
cat("\n-- Items that are not significant --\n")
print(as.data.frame(lv %>% filter(p_holm >= .05) %>% arrange(p_raw) %>%
        select(node, item, value_type, d, d_lo, d_hi, p_raw, p_holm)),
      row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

## Report Table A7

         p_raw, p_holm, p_bonf)
write.csv(table2, file.path(OUT, "table2_level_test.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 3.3 Exploratory edge-level tests (4200 edges)

```{r g2-edges}
ed <- read.csv(find_csv("nct_edges_exploratory_all20.csv"))
stopifnot(nrow(ed) == 20 * N_EDGES)
## Label self-check: item1/item2 must hold real item names, not V numbers
stopifnot(!any(grepl("^V[0-9]+$", ed$item1)), all(ed$item1 %in% ITEMS))

show("Edge tests in total", nrow(ed), " (20 countries x ", N_EDGES, " edges)")
show("Smallest raw p", signif(min(ed$p_edge_raw), 4),
     " (= 1/1001, the resolution limit at 1000 permutations)")
show("Edges reaching that resolution limit", sum(ed$p_edge_raw <= 1/1001 + 1e-12))
show("Edges with raw p < .05", sum(ed$p_edge_raw < .05),
     sprintf(" (%.1f%%, against about 5%% expected by chance)", 100 * mean(ed$p_edge_raw < .05)))
show("Edges with p < .05 after Holm correction within country", sum(ed$p_edge_holm_within_country < .05))
show("Edges with p < .05 after Holm correction across all 4200 tests", sum(ed$p_edge_holm_all_4200 < .05))
show("Smallest within-country Holm p", sprintf("%.3f (%s)", min(ed$p_edge_holm_within_country),
     ed$cntry[which.min(ed$p_edge_holm_within_country)]))

cat("\n-- Five largest absolute changes among all 4200 edges --\n")
print(as.data.frame(ed %>% slice_max(abs_delta, n = 5) %>%
        select(cntry, item1, item2, delta_R10_minus_R9, p_edge_raw,
               p_edge_holm_within_country)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

cat("-- The largest change in Hungary and in Estonia --\n")
hu_ee <- ed %>% filter(cntry %in% c("HU", "EE")) %>% group_by(cntry) %>%
  slice_max(abs_delta, n = 1) %>% ungroup()
print(as.data.frame(hu_ee %>% select(cntry, item1, item2, delta_R10_minus_R9,
                                     p_edge_raw, p_edge_holm_within_country)),
      row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

## Key cross-check: the NCT M statistic IS the largest absolute edge difference, so it must match the table above
cat("\n-- Cross-check: M statistic equals each country's largest absolute edge difference --\n")
chk <- ed %>% group_by(cntry) %>% summarise(max_abs_delta = max(abs_delta), .groups = "drop") %>%
  left_join(nct %>% select(cntry, M), by = "cntry") %>%
  mutate(diff = abs(max_abs_delta - M))
show("Largest |max_abs_delta - M| across the 20 countries", signif(max(chk$diff), 3))

## Count of edges with raw p < .05 per country. Descriptive only, and never used to rank countries
edge_ct <- ed %>% group_by(cntry) %>%
  summarise(n_raw_p05 = sum(p_edge_raw < .05), min_p = min(p_edge_raw),
            max_abs_delta = max(abs_delta), median_abs_delta = median(abs_delta),
            .groups = "drop") %>% arrange(desc(n_raw_p05))
print(as.data.frame(edge_ct), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
write.csv(edge_ct, file.path(OUT, "table_edge_nct_by_country.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 3.4 Common patterns across countries, and cross-national heterogeneity

```{r g2-crosscountry}
csedge <- read.csv(find_csv("cross_country_signed_edge_changes.csv"))
cp     <- read.csv(find_csv("country_change_patterns_20.csv"))
dsp    <- read.csv(find_csv("display_country_selection.csv"))
stopifnot(nrow(csedge) == N_EDGES, nrow(cp) == 20, nrow(dsp) == 20)

show("Edges whose median change is exactly 0", sum(csedge$median_delta == 0),
     sprintf(" (%.1f%%, meaning most edges show no estimated change in most countries)",
             100 * mean(csedge$median_delta == 0)))

cat("\n-- Edges moving in the same direction in 17 or more countries --\n")
common <- csedge %>% filter(n_positive_change >= 17 | n_negative_change >= 17) %>%
  select(item1, item2, median_delta, mean_delta, n_positive_change,
         n_negative_change, n_no_change)
print(as.data.frame(common), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

cat("-- Three edges with the largest mean absolute change across countries --\n")
print(as.data.frame(csedge %>% slice_max(mean_abs_delta, n = 3) %>%
        select(item1, item2, mean_delta, mean_abs_delta, min_delta, max_delta)),
      row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

show("Edges with no change, per country", sprintf("range %d to %d, median %g",
     min(cp$n_no_change), max(cp$n_no_change), median(cp$n_no_change)))

## Ranking by Euclidean distance from the median change pattern. Descriptive, not a significance ranking
show("Distance range", sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", min(cp$distance_to_median_pattern),
                          max(cp$distance_to_median_pattern)))
cat("\n-- The 3 countries closest to and the 3 furthest from the median change pattern --\n")
print(as.data.frame(dsp %>% filter(case_group != "Middle") %>%
        select(cntry, distance_to_median_pattern, distance_rank, case_group)),
      row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)
cat("-- Where the two countries with significant structure tests fall in the distance ranking, showing that significance and magnitude of change are separate questions --\n")
print(as.data.frame(dsp %>% filter(cntry %in% c("HU", "EE")) %>%
        select(cntry, distance_rank, distance_to_median_pattern)), row.names = FALSE, digits = 4)

## Magnitude of change and distance from the common pattern, country by country
table5 <- cp %>% select(cntry, mean_abs_edge_change, max_abs_edge_change, l2_change,
                        distance_to_median_pattern, n_positive_change,
                        n_negative_change, n_no_change) %>%
  left_join(dsp %>% select(cntry, distance_rank, case_group), by = "cntry") %>%
  arrange(distance_rank)
print(as.data.frame(table5), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
write.csv(table5, file.path(OUT, "table5_country_change_patterns.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## Appendix Table A17: the report gives only the range of distances, and the full 20-country ranking goes in the appendix
tableA17 <- table5 %>%
  transmute(Country = cntry,
            Rank = distance_rank,
            Distance = sprintf("%.3f", distance_to_median_pattern),
            `Mean absolute edge change` = sprintf("%.3f", mean_abs_edge_change))
print(as.data.frame(tableA17), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(tableA17, file.path(OUT, "tableA17_distance_to_median_pattern.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```

## 5. Drawing the figures used in the report

The forest plot, the three-panel appendix figure and the edge-precision plots were produced in Part 1.
This section draws the remaining figures of the report from the CSV files read above. Figure numbers appear only in the figure titles and in the report text,
while the output files carry descriptive names, so that inserting a new figure never requires renaming a file.

On colour: positive and negative directions use a blue (`#2a78d6`) and red (`#e34948`) diverging pair, matching the `posCol`/`negCol` convention of the project qgraph network figures.
Where direction does not need to be distinguished, a single blue is used, and secondary objects recede in neutral grey (`#6f6e6a`).
The blue/red pair was checked against colour-vision-deficiency simulation: the worst pairing has a perceptual difference of 21.6 (protan) and 32.3 in normal vision, both far above threshold.
Countries of interest are additionally labelled directly, so that nothing depends on colour alone.

```{r g2-heterogeneity}
## ---- Objective 2, supplementary: where in the value system the changes fall, and whether countries share one pattern ------------------
ee <- read.csv(find_csv("nct_edges_exploratory_all20.csv")) %>%
  left_join(ITEM_MAP %>% select(item, h1 = higher_order), by = c("item1" = "item")) %>%
  left_join(ITEM_MAP %>% select(item, h2 = higher_order), by = c("item2" = "item"))

cat("\n-- Mean absolute change across countries, grouped by higher-order value pair --\n")
grp <- ee %>%
  mutate(pair = ifelse(h1 < h2, paste(h1, h2, sep = " - "), paste(h2, h1, sep = " - "))) %>%
  group_by(pair) %>%
  summarise(n_edges = n() / 20, mean_abs = mean(abs_delta), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abs))
print(as.data.frame(grp), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)

cat("\n-- Pairwise correlations between the countries' edge-change vectors --\n")
wide <- ee %>% mutate(key = paste(node1, node2)) %>%
  select(cntry, key, delta_R10_minus_R9) %>%
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = cntry, values_from = delta_R10_minus_R9)
CM <- cor(as.matrix(wide[, -1])); ut <- upper.tri(CM)
show("Median pairwise correlation", sprintf("%.3f", median(CM[ut])),
     ", range ", sprintf("%.3f to %.3f", min(CM[ut]), max(CM[ut])),
     ", over ", sum(ut), " pairs")
hi <- which(CM == max(CM[ut]), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
lo <- which(CM == min(CM[ut]), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
show("Most similar pair", paste(colnames(CM)[hi], collapse = " / "), sprintf(" (%.3f)", max(CM[ut])))
show("Least similar pair", paste(colnames(CM)[lo], collapse = " / "), sprintf(" (%.3f)", min(CM[ut])))

cat("\n-- The three edges with the largest mean absolute change, direction by country --\n")
top3 <- csedge %>% arrange(desc(mean_abs_delta)) %>% slice(1:3)
for (k in seq_len(nrow(top3))) {
  sub <- ee %>%
    filter((item1 == top3$item1[k] & item2 == top3$item2[k]) |
           (item1 == top3$item2[k] & item2 == top3$item1[k])) %>%
    arrange(delta_R10_minus_R9)
  cat(sprintf("%s - %s | up in %d countries, down in %d, unchanged in %d\n",
              top3$item1[k], top3$item2[k],
              sum(sub$delta_R10_minus_R9 > 0), sum(sub$delta_R10_minus_R9 < 0),
              sum(sub$delta_R10_minus_R9 == 0)))
  cat("   Largest decreases: ", paste(sprintf("%s %.3f", head(sub$cntry, 3),
                                     head(sub$delta_R10_minus_R9, 3)), collapse = ", "), "\n")
  cat("   Largest increases: ", paste(sprintf("%s %.3f", rev(tail(sub$cntry, 3)),
                                     rev(tail(sub$delta_R10_minus_R9, 3))), collapse = ", "), "\n")
}

cat("\n-- Magnitude of change and the balance of positive and negative edges, by country --\n")
print(as.data.frame(cp %>%
  select(cntry, mean_abs_edge_change, n_positive_change, n_negative_change,
         n_no_change, distance_to_median_pattern) %>%
  arrange(desc(mean_abs_edge_change))), row.names = FALSE, digits = 3)
```

```{r g3-comembership}
## ---- Objective 3, supplementary: how the items cluster ------------------------------------------------
co <- st %>% filter(!is.na(empirical_community)) %>%
  select(cntry, wave, item, empirical_community)
nets <- unique(paste(co$cntry, co$wave)); its <- sort(unique(co$item))
P <- matrix(0, length(its), length(its), dimnames = list(its, its)); NN <- P
for (nn in nets) {
  pp <- strsplit(nn, " ")[[1]]
  v <- co %>% filter(cntry == pp[1], wave == pp[2])
  vv <- setNames(v$empirical_community, v$item); ii <- names(vv)
  for (a in ii) for (b in ii) { NN[a, b] <- NN[a, b] + 1
                                if (vv[a] == vv[b]) P[a, b] <- P[a, b] + 1 }
}
RR <- P / NN; ut <- upper.tri(RR)
ho <- setNames(ITEM_MAP$higher_order, ITEM_MAP$item)
vt <- setNames(ITEM_MAP$value_type,  ITEM_MAP$item)
show("Item pairs from the same basic value, mean co-membership rate",
     sprintf("%.3f", mean(RR[ut & outer(vt[its], vt[its], "==")])))
show("Item pairs from the same higher-order value, mean co-membership rate",
     sprintf("%.3f", mean(RR[ut & outer(ho[its], ho[its], "==")])))
show("Item pairs from different higher-order values, mean co-membership rate",
     sprintf("%.3f", mean(RR[ut & !outer(ho[its], ho[its], "==")])))
dd <- data.frame(a = its[row(RR)[ut]], b = its[col(RR)[ut]], r = RR[ut])
cat("\n-- Item pairs that share a community in all 40 networks --\n"); print(dd %>% filter(r == 1), row.names = FALSE)
show("Item pairs that never share a community", sum(dd$r == 0), " / ", nrow(dd))

cat("\n-- Distribution of community counts, and the higher-order composition of each solution --\n")
kk <- co %>% group_by(cntry, wave) %>%
  summarise(K = n_distinct(empirical_community), .groups = "drop")
print(table(n_communities = kk$K))
sig_of <- function(K) {
  nets2 <- kk %>% filter(K == !!K); sig <- character(0)
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(nets2))) {
    v <- co %>% filter(cntry == nets2$cntry[i], wave == nets2$wave[i])
    lab <- sapply(split(v$item, v$empirical_community),
                  function(g) paste(sort(unique(ho[g])), collapse = "+"))
    sig <- c(sig, paste(sort(lab), collapse = " || "))
  }
  sort(table(sig), decreasing = TRUE)
}
for (K in c(2, 4)) { cat("\nK =", K, "\n"); print(head(sig_of(K), 3)) }

cat("\n-- Community composition by round for the four countries shown in Figure 6 --\n")
for (cc2 in c("FI", "HU", "IT", "SI")) for (w in c("R9", "R10")) {
  v <- co %>% filter(cntry == cc2, wave == w)
  cat(cc2, w, ": ", paste(sapply(split(v$item, v$empirical_community),
      function(g) paste(g, collapse = ",")), collapse = " | "), "\n", sep = "")
}
```

```{r figures, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
## ---- Figure 4: standardised round differences in the 21 items ------------------------------------------
## Blue marks items significant after Holm correction, grey those that are not. The pairing was checked for colour-vision deficiency (separation 17.0 under protan simulation).
## The intervals are per-item 95% CIs with no simultaneous correction, so an interval can exclude zero while the item is not significant after correction. The caption says so as well.
d_lvl <- read.csv(file.path(ROOT, "level_test_weighted.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(lab = paste0(unname(ITEM_EN[item]), "  (", item, ")"),
         sig = ifelse(p_holm < .05, "Holm-adjusted p < .05", "Not significant")) %>%
  arrange(d) %>%
  mutate(lab = factor(lab, levels = lab))
n_sig <- sum(d_lvl$p_holm < .05); n_up <- sum(d_lvl$p_holm < .05 & d_lvl$d > 0)

p_lvl <- ggplot(d_lvl, aes(x = d, y = lab, colour = sig)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 0, colour = "grey55", linewidth = 0.4) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = d_lo, xmax = d_hi), height = 0, linewidth = 0.7) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Holm-adjusted p < .05" = BLUE, "Not significant" = GREY)) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-0.13, 0.22), breaks = seq(-0.10, 0.20, 0.05)) +
  labs(title = "Figure 4. Standardised round differences in the 21 value items",
       subtitle = "Survey-weighted regression with country fixed effects, R10 minus R9, with 95% confidence intervals",
       x = "Standardised difference (R10 - R9)", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0(
         "Positive values mean higher endorsement in R10. ", n_sig,
         " of the 21 items differ after Holm correction\nacross the 21 tests, ", n_up,
         " of them upward. The intervals are the 95% CI for each item on its own and are not\n",
         "adjusted for multiplicity, so an interval can exclude zero while the item is not significant after correction.")) +
  theme_thesis +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(colour = "#3d3c39"))
save_fig(file.path(FIG, "fig_level_forest.png"), p_lvl, width = 9.2, height = 7)
p_lvl

## ---- Figure 5: overall structure test for the 20 countries -------------------------------------------
d2 <- nct %>%
  mutate(sig = ifelse(p_struct_holm < .05, "Holm-adjusted p < .05", "Not significant"),
         lab = ifelse(p_struct_holm < .05,
                      sprintf("%s  M = %.3f, p = %.3f", cntry, M, p_struct_holm), NA))
p2 <- ggplot(d2, aes(x = M, y = reorder(cntry, M), colour = sig)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = M, yend = reorder(cntry, M)), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  geom_text(aes(label = lab), hjust = -0.06, size = 3, show.legend = FALSE, na.rm = TRUE) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Holm-adjusted p < .05" = BLUE, "Not significant" = GREY)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.42))) +
  labs(title = "Figure 5. Network structure invariance test (NCT), 20 countries",
       subtitle = "M = maximum absolute edge-weight difference between R9 and R10; 1,000 permutations",
       x = "M statistic", y = NULL,
       caption = "Holm correction applied across the 20 countries. Only Hungary and Estonia reject structural equality.") +
  theme_thesis
save_fig(file.path(FIG, "fig_nct_structure.png"), p2)
p2

## ---- Appendix Figure D1: Euclidean distance from the median change pattern ------------------------------------
## Country identity is already given by the y axis, so colour encodes only the three groups (closest, middle, furthest) rather than repeating the country codes
d4 <- dsp %>%
  mutate(grp = factor(case_group, levels = c("Closest 3", "Middle", "Farthest 3")))
p4 <- ggplot(d4, aes(x = distance_to_median_pattern, y = reorder(cntry, -distance_rank),
                     colour = grp)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = min(d4$distance_to_median_pattern) * 0.97,
                   xend = distance_to_median_pattern,
                   yend = reorder(cntry, -distance_rank)), linewidth = 0.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Closest 3" = BLUE, "Middle" = GREY, "Farthest 3" = RED)) +
  scale_x_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0, 0.04))) +
  labs(title = "Appendix Figure D1. Distance from the 20-country median edge-change pattern",
       subtitle = "Euclidean distance over the 210-dimensional signed edge-change vector, descriptive only",
       x = "Euclidean distance to median change pattern", y = NULL,
       caption = paste0("Distance ranks how far a country edge-change pattern lies from the ",
                        "20-country median, not statistical significance.\nHungary and Estonia, the ",
                        "only two countries with significant structural change, rank 17th and 6th.")) +
  theme_thesis
save_fig(file.path(FIG, "fig_distance_rank.png"), p4, width = 8.6, height = 6.4)
p4

## ---- Figure 6: community partitions in both rounds for four countries --------------------------------------------
## The categorical palette (blue/orange/aqua/yellow) was checked for colour-vision deficiency; the worst adjacent pairing separates by 9.1 under protan simulation.
## That is below a 3:1 contrast ratio, so each cell also carries its community number as redundant encoding.
COMM_PAL <- c("Openness" = "#2a78d6", "Self-enhancement" = "#eb6834",
              "Conservation" = "#1baf7a", "Self-transcendence" = "#eda100")
HO_ORDER <- names(COMM_PAL)
SEL_C <- c("FI", "HU", "IT", "SI")
SEL_LAB <- c(FI = "Finland   ARI = 1.000", HU = "Hungary   ARI = 0.809",
             IT = "Italy   ARI = 0.693",  SI = "Slovenia   ARI = 0.422")

dc <- st %>% filter(cntry %in% SEL_C) %>%
  left_join(ITEM_MAP %>% select(item, item_en, value_type, higher_order), by = "item") %>%
  group_by(cntry, wave, empirical_community) %>%
  mutate(comm_ho = names(sort(table(higher_order), decreasing = TRUE))[1]) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(comm_ho = ifelse(is.na(empirical_community), NA_character_, comm_ho),
         comm_ho = factor(comm_ho, levels = HO_ORDER),
         wave    = factor(wave, levels = c("R9", "R10")),
         cntry   = factor(cntry, levels = SEL_C, labels = SEL_LAB[SEL_C]),
         lab_left = sprintf("%s  (%s)", item_en, item))

ord_c <- ITEM_MAP %>%
  mutate(ho = factor(higher_order, levels = HO_ORDER),
         lab_left = sprintf("%s  (%s)", item_en, item)) %>%
  arrange(desc(as.integer(ho)), value_type, item_en)
dc$lab_left <- factor(dc$lab_left, levels = ord_c$lab_left)

p_comm <- ggplot(dc, aes(x = wave, y = lab_left, fill = comm_ho)) +
  geom_tile(colour = "#fcfcfb", linewidth = 1.6) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ifelse(is.na(empirical_community), "-",
                               as.character(empirical_community))),
            size = 2.7, colour = "#0b0b0b") +
  facet_wrap(~ cntry, nrow = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = COMM_PAL, na.value = "#d9d8d2",
                    breaks = HO_ORDER, drop = FALSE,
                    name = "Higher-order value dominating the community") +
  scale_x_discrete(position = "top", expand = c(0, 0)) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL,
       caption = paste("Cell numbers are community labels within one network only.",
                       "Items are ordered by their theoretical higher-order value.")) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9) +
  theme(panel.grid = element_blank(), legend.position = "bottom",
        legend.key.size = unit(9, "pt"),
        strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 9),
        axis.text.x.top = element_text(size = 8.5),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size = 7.6),
        plot.caption = element_text(hjust = 0, colour = "#52514e", size = 7.2),
        plot.margin = margin(6, 10, 6, 6))
save_fig(file.path(FIG, "fig_community_examples.png"), p_comm, width = 10.2, height = 4.8)
p_comm
```
